items.title: Aurelius Atlas
items.text:
Data governance made simple. Aurelius Atlas is an open-source data governance solution that enables business users to find, understand, and trust their data without waiting on IT: discover data assets and their context in seconds, see who is accountable for them and whether they are fit for purpose, follow the journey and transformations of data across systems, and keep sensitive information in line with regulations such as GDPR.

It is one all-in-one data catalogue, designed to be business-user-friendly, meeting the demands of modern distributed data environments.

This repository builds the new engine behind that product: a Python re-implementation of Apache Atlas that keeps the Atlas 2.4.0 REST API and the Atlas dashboard, with Elasticsearch 9 as the only backend instead of JanusGraph, HBase and Solr — so the catalogue is far easier to run and cheaper to operate. The original Java Atlas is converted in small, reviewed increments, each proven against the Atlas 2.4.0 source code, so the clients, integrations, and dashboards organisations rely on keep working exactly as they do today.

Start with the User Guide for what the catalogue does for your organisation, the Conversion roadmap for plan and status, the Architecture overview for the system as it will stand, and the Contributor Guide to set up your machine.

The User Guide is intentionally short: until the conversion is complete, the Apache Atlas documentation describes the behaviour this system reproduces, and every intended difference is listed in Deviations from Apache Atlas.

items.title: About the team
items.text: This project is maintained by the Aurelius Enterprise team. Please feel free to reach out if you have any questions, need assistance, or would like to contribute.

items.title: API Reference
items.text:
Generated API documentation for the Aurelius Atlas workspace, rendered from the docstrings in each project by mkdocstrings. The prose for what a project is lives in its README.md; the wiring for how it is built and run lives in its AGENTS.md (ADR 003). This tree is the reference for what it exposes: classes, functions, signatures, and examples.

Each page doubles as that component's design documentation: the technology-specific detail of how the component works — settings and knob names, storage layout, protocol mechanics, ports, commands. The architecture trees state the technology-neutral properties the component must keep. A page's Design section carries this detail, with the ADR that owns each rule linked.

  • Apps — the services: the Atlas server and the auxiliary APIs
  • Libs — the Python, Angular, and style libraries the apps consume

items.title: Apps
items.text: API reference for the workspace applications. The Atlas product is aurelius-atlas-server. The template's example apps left when the Atlas server and webapp replaced them (ADR 050).

items.title: aurelius-atlas-server
items.text: The Aurelius Atlas server: the Apache Atlas 2.4.0 REST API on Elasticsearch.

items.title: Usage
items.text:
npx nx serve aurelius-atlas-server

This starts the dev Elasticsearch store and the observability stack, then the server at https://localhost:21000, the port Apache Atlas uses.

items.title: Deployment
items.text: Deploy the image built from the provided Dockerfile. It listens on port 21000 and needs the Elasticsearch settings; it does not start without its store.

PEM CA verifying the provider's TLS; unset uses the system trust store.

items.title: auth_client_id pydantic-field

auth_client_id: str = 'aurelius-atlas-server'

The server's confidential client: browsers sign in with it, and its tokens are accepted (AUT-05).

The secret of auth_client_id; never shown in logs.

The claim a user's groups are read from, else the realm roles: atlas.authentication.method.keycloak .groups_claim (AUT-03).

items.title: auth_principal_claim pydantic-field
items.text:
auth_principal_claim: str = 'preferred_username'

The claim a user's name is read from: Atlas's Keycloak principal-attribute (AUT-03, DD-250).

items.title: auth_realm pydantic-field

auth_realm: str = 'master'

The realm the tokens are issued from.

items.title: auth_server_url pydantic-field

The identity provider's root (Keycloak), which tokens are verified against and browsers sign in at (AUT-02, AUT-05; ADR 007).

items.title: cluster_name pydantic-field
items.text:
cluster_name: str = 'default'

The cluster an export says it comes from: atlas.metadata.namespace, else atlas.cluster.name (EXP-06).

items.title: dashboard_dir pydantic-field
items.text:
dashboard_dir: DirectoryPath | None = None

The built dashboards: dashboardv2 at its root and dashboardv3 in n/; None serves the API only (DSH-04).

items.title: delete_type pydantic-field
items.text:
delete_type: Literal['soft', 'hard'] = 'soft'

How entities are deleted unless a request chooses: atlas.DeleteHandlerV1.impl (EDL-04, DD-059).

items.title: delete_type_override pydantic-field
items.text:
delete_type_override: bool = False

Whether a request's deleteType chooses: atlas.rest.enable.delete.type.override (EDL-04, DD-059).

items.title: elasticsearch_ca_certs pydantic-field
items.text:
elasticsearch_ca_certs: FilePath

PEM file with the certificate authority of the Elasticsearch server certificate.

items.title: elasticsearch_hosts pydantic-field
items.text:
elasticsearch_hosts: list[HttpUrl]

Base URLs of the Elasticsearch nodes, as a JSON list: ["https://localhost:9200"].

items.title: elasticsearch_password pydantic-field
items.text:
elasticsearch_password: SecretStr

Password for the store; never shown in logs.

items.title: elasticsearch_username pydantic-field
items.text:
elasticsearch_username: str = 'elastic'

User for the store.

items.title: forwarded_allow_ips pydantic-field
items.text:
forwarded_allow_ips: str = '127.0.0.1'

Which peers may rewrite the client address through X-Forwarded-For (SRV-10, DD-238), passed to uvicorn. The default trusts only the loopback; behind a proxy the arrangement names the proxy network, so the access log and OTel peer attributes key on the browser's address, not the proxy's. The rate limit itself lives at the webapp's nginx edge, not here (SRV-09, DD-238).

items.title: host pydantic-field
items.text:
host: str = 'localhost'

The interface to listen on; the container image sets 0.0.0.0.

items.title: hsts_enabled pydantic-field
items.text:
hsts_enabled: bool = True

Whether responses carry Strict-Transport-Security (SRV-08, DD-236). The image ships True; the dev arrangement turns it off so a browser that visited the mkcert server is not pinned to HTTPS on the plaintext dev surfaces (ADR 039's named relaxations).

items.title: import_folder pydantic-field
items.text:
import_folder: Path | None = None

The one folder admin/importfile reads export ZIPs from; none refuses every file (IMS-06, DV-125).

items.title: lineage_max_node_count pydantic-field
items.text:
lineage_max_node_count: int = 9000

The relations past which lineage adds none (at most 9,000): atlas.lineage.max.node.count (LIN-04).

items.title: lineage_on_demand_default_node_count pydantic-field
items.text:
lineage_on_demand_default_node_count: int = 3

The relations each way lineage on demand takes by default: atlas.lineage.on.demand.default.node.count (LIN-06).

items.title: lineage_on_demand_enabled pydantic-field
items.text:
lineage_on_demand_enabled: bool = False

Whether POST v2/lineage/{guid} answers lineage on demand: atlas.lineage.on.demand.enabled (LIN-06).

items.title: log_level pydantic-field
items.text:
log_level: LogLevel = 'info'

The lowest level of log record the server and uvicorn emit.

items.title: model_config class-attribute instance-attribute
items.text: model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix=ENV_PREFIX, frozen=True, extra='ignore')

items.title: models_dir pydantic-field
items.text:
models_dir: Path = BUILTIN_MODELS_DIR

The models loaded at start-up: by default addons/models of Apache Atlas 2.4.0; a missing directory loads none (MDL-01, MDL-16, DD-032).

items.title: otel_ca_file pydantic-field
items.text:
otel_ca_file: FilePath | None = None

PEM CA verifying the collector's TLS for the OTLP export; unset uses the system trust store (the dev stack's mkcert CA is not system-wide).

items.title: otel_client_id pydantic-field
items.text:
otel_client_id: str = 'otel-atlas-server'

The ingest realm client the server mints for (7.18, DD-196).

items.title: otel_client_secret pydantic-field
items.text:
otel_client_secret: SecretStr | None = None

The secret of otel_client_id; never shown in logs.

items.title: otel_endpoint pydantic-field
items.text:
otel_endpoint: str = 'https://localhost:4319'

The collector's per-service-leg HTTP base for the OTLP export (7.18, DD-196); the dev compose overrides with the service DNS name.

items.title: otel_token_url pydantic-field
items.text:
otel_token_url: HttpUrl | None = None

The issuer's token endpoint for the OTLP ingest credential (7.18, DD-196): with otel_client_secret set, the server exports OTLP through the app-owned pipeline (the collector's per-service leg accepts only client-credentials JWTs); unset, the server exports no OTLP (console only). The OTel env vars (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*) are deliberately not read: the 60s dev token cannot ride a static header (DD-196).

items.title: port pydantic-field
items.text:
port: int = DEFAULT_PORT

The port to listen on (SRV-03).

items.title: revision pydantic-field
items.text:
revision: str = 'UNKNOWN'

The source revision the server was built from, reported by admin/version (ADM-01).

items.title: session_timeout_seconds pydantic-field
items.text:
session_timeout_seconds: int = 3600

How long a browser session lasts unused: Atlas's web.xml session timeout, 60 minutes (AUT-06).

items.title: task_poll_seconds pydantic-field
items.text:
task_poll_seconds: float = 10.0

How often the worker looks for tasks other processes recorded or left behind (DD-080).

items.title: tasks_enabled pydantic-field
items.text:
tasks_enabled: bool = True

Whether propagation is deferred to tasks a worker runs after the request: atlas.tasks.enabled (TSK-02, DD-081).

items.title: tls property
items.text:
tls: tuple[Path, Path]

The certificate and key to serve HTTPS with (SRV-03, SRV-06, DD-234).

items.title: tls_cert_file pydantic-field
items.text:
tls_cert_file: FilePath

PEM certificate to serve HTTPS with (SRV-06, DD-234): required — the server never serves plaintext, the way the store's password is required (SRV-01, SRV-02).

items.title: tls_key_file pydantic-field
items.text:
tls_key_file: FilePath

PEM private key of tls_cert_file (SRV-06).

items.title: typedef_refresh_seconds pydantic-field
items.text:
typedef_refresh_seconds: float = 5.0

How long the server answers from its type registry before it checks for another process's type change (TDS-13, DD-029).

items.title: store_settings
items.text:
store_settings() -> StoreSettings

The settings of the Elasticsearch store.

items.title: Design
items.text:
The technology-specific detail of how the server runs. The properties it must keep are in the architecture: Configuration Management (ADR 018), Components & Interfaces.

Settings. Read once at start-up into a frozen ServerSettings; a validation failure (missing key, bad scheme, missing TLS material) stops start-up with a message naming the variable (SRV-01, SRV-02, SRV-06). All names carry the AURELIUS_ATLAS_SERVER_ prefix. What a deployment must supply, with no defaults:

Variable Purpose ..._ELASTICSEARCH_HOSTS JSON list of store node URLs, e.g. ["https://es-0:9200"] — https only ..._ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD Store password — a SecretStr, never shown in logs ..._ELASTICSEARCH_CA_CERTS PEM CA of the store certificate; the store link is https-only (ADR 039) ..._TLS_CERT_FILE + ..._TLS_KEY_FILE PEM pair for serving HTTPS: both required — the server never serves plaintext (SRV-06, DD-234)

With defaults: HOST (0.0.0.0 in the image), PORT (21000, Atlas's port — kept so existing clients find the catalogue where Atlas was, ADR 046), LOG_LEVEL, REVISION (reported by admin/version, ADM-01), HSTS_ENABLED (true — the dev arrangement sets it false, SRV-08/DD-236), DASHBOARD_DIR (None serves the API only, DSH-04), MODELS_DIR (default: the vendored Atlas 2.4.0 addons/models, MDL-16/DD-032), TYPEDEF_REFRESH_SECONDS (5.0 — how long the server answers from its type registry before checking for another process's type change, TDS-13/DD-029).

The server does not start without TLS material

TLS_CERT_FILE and TLS_KEY_FILE are required settings — there is no plaintext mode (SRV-06, DD-234, superseding the both-or-neither rule of SRV-03). A container that mounts no material exits with a message naming the missing variable; this is the design working, not a broken image. The image's ENV names where the pair lives (/certs/server.pem, /certs/server-key.pem — DD-216's stack-owned mount).

The image (apps/aurelius-atlas-server/Dockerfile: hardened base, runs as nonroot) bakes in the production defaults — listen on 0.0.0.0:21000, dashboards served from /application/dashboard — and a liveness healthcheck against /api/atlas/admin/liveness over HTTPS, verifying the served certificate (SRV-06). Liveness is the probe a restart decision uses; readiness also fails while the store is away (DD-016).

Security headers. Every answer carries them (SRV-08, DD-236): security_headers.py stamps the JSON API with no-store/nosniff/framing-closed headers and a documents-free CSP, the dashboards with a same-origin CSP (DV-86) and immutable caching on bust-versioned assets, and HSTS when HSTS_ENABLED.

Parity scenarios. scenarios/<resource>/*.scenario.yaml state each expectation as Atlas's own answer — e.g. scenarios/admin/version.scenario.yaml expects Version: "2.4.0", Name: apache-atlas, the exact content type — each cited to the Java source that produces it. Build-varying fields are marked volatile; the two places Aurelius Atlas must answer differently (name, description) carry a deviations: DV-03 entry. Anything else that differs fails the scenario (ADR 052).

items.title: aurelius_atlas_server.app
items.text:
The FastAPI application: settings, the store's lifetime, error handling and routers (DD-015, DD-016).

Functions:

  • build_auth –

    The token verifier: the provider's tokens for the server's client and the further audiences (AUT-02).

  • build_oidc –

    The server's client at the provider, which browsers sign in with (AUT-05).

  • create_app –

    Build the application.

  • mount_dashboards –

    Serve dashboardv3 at /n/ and dashboardv2 at / (DSH-01, DSH-02; DD-018).

Attributes:

  • DASHBOARD_V3_DIR –

    Where dashboardv3 sits in the dashboard directory, and below which path it is served.

  • LOGGER –
  • NAME –

items.text:
DASHBOARD_V3_DIR = 'n'

Where dashboardv3 sits in the dashboard directory, and below which path it is served.

items.title: build_auth
items.text:
build_auth(settings: ServerSettings, http: Client | None = None) -> KeycloakAuth

The token verifier: the provider's tokens for the server's client and the further audiences (AUT-02).

items.title: build_oidc
items.text:
build_oidc(settings: ServerSettings, auth: KeycloakAuth, http: AsyncClient | None = None) -> OidcClient

The server's client at the provider, which browsers sign in with (AUT-05).

items.title: create_app
items.text:
create_app(
    settings: ServerSettings,
    store: ElasticsearchStore | None = None,
    *,
    auth: KeycloakAuth | None = None,
    oidc_http: AsyncClient | None = None,
) -> FastAPI

Build the application.

Parameters:

The type registry is loaded from the stored type definitions when the application starts (TDS-12), then the models are loaded and patched (MDL-16); the entity store's indices are created and interrupted writes recovered (ENS-01, ENS-07), and the audit index (DD-082). With tasks enabled, a worker runs the tasks requests record (TSK-04, DD-080).

items.title: settings
items.text:
(ServerSettings) –

The server's settings.

items.title: store
items.text:
(ElasticsearchStore | None, default: None ) –

The store to use; by default one built from the settings. It is opened when the application starts, which fails when the store cannot be opened (SRV-02), and closed when it stops.

items.title: atlas_error_handler async
items.text:
atlas_error_handler(_request: Request, error: Exception) -> AtlasJSONResponse

Answer an AtlasError with its status and {"errorCode", "errorMessage"[, "errorCause"]} (SRV-04).

A server error (5xx) keeps Atlas's two-field shape and adds the trace id of the request as requestId (SRV-07, DD-235): the cause's text goes to the log, never to the wire, so a wrapped store or transport failure cannot leak internals; the id ties the response to the logged stack and the trace. A client error (4xx) echoes the cause as Atlas does (SRV-04) — there the cause is the request's own defect, not server internals.

items.title: aurelius_atlas_auth.auth
items.text:
Keycloak bearer-token authentication for Aurelius Atlas services (8.0, DD-197).

Ported from the template's FastAPI example (since removed, ADR 050), reshaped as a per-service object so each application owns one :class:KeycloakAuth built from its own settings — no module-level caches shared across applications.

The verification story (AUX-02..AUX-05):

  • OIDC discovery and JWKS are fetched through a circuit breaker (a Keycloak outage is a 503, not a hang) and cached for an hour.
  • Tokens are verified with PyJWT by kid: RS256 signature, issuer and expiry. The audience is checked after decoding against the union of the azp and aud claims, which pyjwt's built-in check cannot express.
  • The write gate accepts the configured role from realm_access.roles or resource_access.<audience>.roles — Keycloak namespaces client roles per client, so only this service's own client entry counts.

  • AuthConfig –

    What a service needs to verify its tokens. Apps map their settings in.

  • KeycloakAuth –

    One service's Keycloak verifier: dependencies for FastAPI routers.

    The roles a token carries of one client, resource_access.<client_id>.roles (AUZ-01).

Attributes:

  • bearer_scheme –

    The scheme every :class:KeycloakAuth shares: one instance keeps FastAPI's

items.title: aurelius-atlas-core
items.text:
Atlas stores and services for Aurelius Atlas (DD-002 (the record: specs/0-1-adopt-template/design.md)). Since increment 1.4 (the spec: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-core/specs/1-4-typedef-store/spec.md): the typedef store, which keeps type definitions in one Elasticsearch document and serves them from the type registry. Since 1.5 (the spec: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-core/specs/1-5-builtin-models/spec.md): Apache Atlas's built-in models and their typedef patches, loaded at start-up. Since 1.6 (the spec: apps/aurelius-atlas-server/specs/1-6-types-rest/spec.md): the store's reads and the search of /v2/types/typedefs. Since 2.2 (the spec: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-core/specs/2-2-entity-store/spec.md): the entity store, which keeps each entity as one Elasticsearch document, reserves unique attribute values and writes several entities all or nothing through a journal (DD-043 to DD-048).

store = TypedefStore(TypeRegistry(), ElasticsearchTypedefDocument(elasticsearch_store.client))
await store.load()  # every stored definition into the registry
created = await store.create_types_def(types_def)
await store.refresh()  # pick up another process's change (at most every 5 s)
await ModelLoader(store).load(BUILTIN_MODELS_DIR)  # addons/models of Atlas 2.4.0, and their patches
store.get_by_name("hive_table")  # the registered definition, as resolution completed it
search_types_def(store.registry, TypeSearchFilter.from_query([("type", "ENTITY")]))  # each kind sorted by name

items.title: aurelius_atlas_core.typedef_store
items.text:
The typedef store: type definitions kept in Elasticsearch and served from the registry (TDS-01 to TDS-13).

Ported from AtlasTypeDefGraphStore and its def stores (Atlas*DefStoreV2) of Apache Atlas 2.4.0. A change is tried on the registry's transient copy, checked as Atlas's def stores check it, written as one document (DD-028) and only then committed to the registry (TDS-10). items.title: apply_patch async
items.text:
apply_patch(patch: AtlasPatch, decide: Callable[[TypeRegistry], PatchChange]) -> PatchStatus | None

Apply a typedef patch unless its record says it is done, and record how it ended (MDL-05, MDL-06).

decide looks at the registry and says what the patch does; an AtlasError from it, or from the update it asks for, makes the patch FAILED, and leaves the definitions as they were. Any other error is raised. The patch's record is written with its change (DD-031); a patch without an id is not recorded.

items.title: aurelius_atlas_core.entity_store
items.text:
EntityStore: entities by GUID and unique attributes, written all or nothing (ENS-02 to ENS-09).

The storage side of AtlasEntityStoreV2 and EntityGraphMapper: what a graph transaction gave Atlas, rebuilt on Elasticsearch with reserved unique values, conditional writes and a journal (DD-044 to DD-048).

  • EntityStore –

items.title: aurelius_atlas_core.entity_documents
items.text:
The entities' documents in Elasticsearch: entities, unique value reservations and the write journal (ENS-01).

The I/O behind EntityStore: reads in real time, conditional writes, create-only reservations (DD-043 to DD-047). Documents go to Elasticsearch as the bytes of Atlas's JSON codec, so values keep their digits (DD-039).

Type Aliases:

  • Linked –

    A document an entity lists: a relationship or a classification instance.

Classes:

  • ElasticsearchEntityDocuments –

    EntityDocuments in three Elasticsearch indices behind aliases (DD-043, DD-045, DD-046).

  • EntityDocuments –

    Where EntityStore keeps entities, reservations and its journal.

  • JournalEntry –

    A write in flight: its id, lease, the entities' states before it, its reservations, releases and removals.

  • LinkedKind –

    The documents an entity lists besides itself, each in an index of its own (DD-061, DD-070).

items.title: aurelius_atlas_core.model_loader
items.text:
Atlas's built-in models and their typedef patches, loaded at start-up (MDL-01 to MDL-15).

Ported from AtlasTypeDefStoreInitializer of Apache Atlas 2.4.0. Each model file and each patch is one change of the typedef store, decided on the newest stored definitions (DD-033); a patch's record is written with its change (DD-031).

Type Aliases:

  • PatchHandler –

Classes:

  • ModelLoad –

    What loading a models directory did: the files that failed, the patch files stopped, each patch's status.

  • ModelLoader –

    Loads a models directory into a typedef store (AtlasTypeDefStoreInitializer.loadBootstrapTypeDefs).

  • PatchDataError –

    Patch data that Atlas does not check, and fails on with a runtime exception (MDL-06, MDL-13).

  • TypedefPatch –

    One typedef patch of a models-directory patch file (MDL-05).

  • TypedefPatches –

    A patch file: the patches of a models directory (MDL-05).

Functions:

  • add_attribute –

    ADD_ATTRIBUTE: add attributes to an entity, classification, struct or relationship (MDL-09).

  • add_mandatory_attribute –

    ADD_MANDATORY_ATTRIBUTE: add mandatory primitive attributes that have a default value (MDL-10).

  • add_super_types –

    ADD_SUPER_TYPES: add super types to an entity type (MDL-14).

  • is_patch_applicable –

    isPatchApplicable: no typeVersion, or applyToVersion ignoring case, or below it (MDL-07).

  • load_plan –

    The model and patch files in the order they load, each with whether it is a patch file (MDL-01).

  • remove_legacy_ref_attributes –

    REMOVE_LEGACY_REF_ATTRIBUTES: move a relationship's legacy attributes to the relationship (MDL-11).

  • set_service_type –

    SET_SERVICE_TYPE: set a type's service type; without one, the update keeps the stored one (MDL-12).

  • sorted_entries –

    The entries of directory by name, compared as File.compareTo does on Unix (MDL-01).

  • update_attribute –

    UPDATE_ATTRIBUTE: replace or add attributes of an entity, classification or struct (MDL-09).

  • update_attribute_metadata –

    UPDATE_ATTRIBUTE_METADATA: set the search weight or index type of an attribute (MDL-13).

  • update_enum_def –

    UPDATE_ENUMDEF: add the elements to an enum (MDL-08).

  • update_typedef_options –

    UPDATE_TYPEDEF_OPTIONS: merge options into a type's options (MDL-12).

Attributes:

  • BUILTIN_MODELS_DIR –

    addons/models of Apache Atlas 2.4.0, unchanged (DD-032).

  • LOGGER –
  • PATCHES_FOLDER_NAME –

    The sub-directory of a models directory that holds its patches.

  • PATCH_HANDLERS (dict[str, PatchHandler]) –

    The patch actions of Atlas 2.4.0 (applyTypePatches, MDL-07 to MDL-14).

  • RACE_ATTEMPTS –

    How often a model file or patch is tried while another process keeps writing first (MDL-15, DD-036).

  • REMOVE_LEGACY_REF_ATTRIBUTES –

    The patch action under which an update may remove attributes and swap a relationship's ends (MDL-11).

items.title: aurelius_atlas_core.typedef_document
items.text:
The stored type definitions: one Elasticsearch document, written with optimistic concurrency (DD-028, DD-029).

Classes:

  • DocumentVersion –

    Which write of the document a reader saw: Elasticsearch's _seq_no and _primary_term (TDS-11).

  • ElasticsearchTypedefDocument –

    The type definitions as one document of the aurelius-atlas-typedefs index (DD-028).

  • StoredTypedefs –

    What the document holds: the definitions, and the record of each typedef patch (DD-028, DD-031).

  • TypedefDocument –

    Where the type definitions are kept.

  • VersionConflictError –

    Another process wrote the document since this one read it (TDS-11).

Attributes:

items.text: The contract and the async client of the data2model extraction API (8.4, DD-203, DD-204): the rules family the legacy chain evolved (AURELIUS-RULES), the extraction request/response, and the Data2ModelClient that posts them. The aurelius-atlas-data2model app imports its own contract from here.

items.title: aurelius_atlas_data2model_client.models
items.text:
The /extract request contract as pydantic models (DTM-01, DTM-11, DTM-12; DD-198).

The legacy chain built these from m4i-analytics dict adapters (ConceptDefinition and subclasses, **kwargs-tolerant); the port states the same fields as pydantic models, so FastAPI validates the public request at the boundary: an unknown concept or relationship type, a missing required key, or a dangling rule reference is a 400 (DTM-11), not a 500 as in the legacy.

The legacy adapters normalise None prefixes/keys to '' — the lineage caller sends nulls for them — so the string fields accept None and normalise to ''; extra keys (alias, description, include, …) are ignored, as the **kwargs did. The tabular data stays a plain list of row maps: the columns are the rules' keys, so the rows are a mapping, not a model (DD-198).

Classes:

  • ElementRule –

    An element rule (legacy ElementDefinition): one node per row of id_key.

  • ExtractionRequest –

    The POST /extract body: {data: [row…], rules: {...}}.

  • ExtractionResponse –

    The POST /extract answer: {metadata: […], model: "<ar3 JSON string>"}.

  • MappingEntry –

    One {key, value}: attach column value as metadata attribute key.

  • MetadataEntry –

    One {id, data} metadata entry of the extraction answer.

  • RelationRule –

    A relation rule (legacy RelationshipDefinition): one edge per row.

  • RulesDef –

    The rules body: elements, relations, views, in rule order.

  • ViewEdgeRule –

    A view edge entry: includes the referenced relation rule's edges.

  • ViewNodeRule –

    A view node entry: includes the referenced element rule's nodes.

  • ViewRule –

    A view rule (legacy ViewDefinition): one diagram per layout match.

Attributes:

  • LegacyStr –

    A legacy string field: null arrives as '', as the legacy adapters normalise it.

  • UNKNOWN_CONCEPT_TYPE_ERROR –

    A concept_type outside the ported type table (DTM-11).

  • UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_RULE_ERROR –

    A relation rule's dangling source/target reference (DTM-11).

  • UNKNOWN_RELATIONSHIP_TYPE_ERROR –

    A relationship_type outside the ported shorthand table (DTM-11).

  • UNKNOWN_VIEW_EDGE_RULE_ERROR –

    A view rule's dangling view_edges reference (DTM-11).

  • UNKNOWN_VIEW_NODE_RULE_ERROR –

    A view rule's dangling view_nodes reference (DTM-11).

items.title: aurelius_atlas_data2model_client.client
items.text:
The async client for the data2model API (CL-01..CL-05, CL-21; DD-203, DD-204, DD-205).

The shared client conventions of increment 8.4: constructed from an externally built httpx.AsyncClient and a token source, reading no environment variables (CL-01) — the app builds the httpx client from its own settings and passes it in. The request path is relative, appended to that client's base URL, so a URL with a trailing slash — the str() of a pydantic HttpUrl — works as given (CL-01); the builder closes the pool, the API client never touches its lifecycle. Tests hand over one built on a MockTransport and no socket opens (CL-02); the bearer token goes on every call (CL-03); :class:Data2ModelClientError rises on a non-2xx answer, with the Atlas-shaped body when it parses (CL-04); an unreachable upstream propagates as httpx's own error (CL-05).

extract posts an :class:~aurelius_atlas_data2model_client.models.ExtractionRequest — the same model class the server validates — and returns an :class:~aurelius_atlas_data2model_client.models.ExtractionResponse, so the 8.2 chain's payload and the 8.1 answer are one contract on both sides (CL-21).

items.title: aurelius-atlas-dsl
items.text:
The Atlas DSL for Aurelius Atlas, without I/O (DD-002 (the record: specs/0-1-adopt-template/design.md)). Since increment 4.3 (the spec: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-dsl/specs/4-3-dsl-parser/spec.md): a query parsed by Atlas's own grammar, with Atlas's syntax errors, into a typed syntax tree; and the clauses, limit and offset it asks for. The parser is generated by ANTLR from Atlas's AtlasDSLLexer.g4 and AtlasDSLParser.g4, unchanged (DD-240 (the record: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-dsl/specs/4-3-dsl-parser/design.md)).

from aurelius_atlas_dsl.atlas_dsl import QueryMetadata, parse

query = parse("hive_table where name = 'sales' select name limit 10")  # raises AtlasError INVALID_DSL_QUERY
query.sources[0].where.expr.comp_e.operator  # Operator.EQ
QueryMetadata.of(query).resolved_limit  # 10

items.title: aurelius_atlas_dsl.dsl_tree
items.text:
The Atlas DSL's parse tree as typed, immutable nodes (DD-241).

One node per rule of AtlasDSLParser.g4 that DSLVisitor reads, named after it; a rule that only chooses (literal, atomE, compE, fromSrc, singleQrySrc) is the union of its alternatives, and querySrc, selectClause, limitClause and offsetClause are folded into their parent. Every node keeps text, the rule's getText(): its tokens joined without the spaces and comments the lexer skipped (DSL-05).

Type Aliases:

  • AtomE –
  • CompE –
  • SingleQrySrc –

Classes:

  • ArithE –

    arithE: a product and the sums after it.

  • ArithERight –

    arithERight: + or - and a product.

  • BoolOperator –

    The connective of an exprRight.

  • ComparisonClause –

    comparisonClause; operator_text is the operator as written (< or lt, any case).

  • CountClause –

    countClause: count().

  • Expr –

    expr: conditions joined left to right, without precedence between and and or.

  • ExprRight –

    exprRight: and or or and the next condition.

  • FromClause –

    fromClause: from and a fromExpression.

  • FromExpression –

    fromExpression: its fromSrc, as source and the alias of an aliasExpr, and its where.

  • Group –

    The ( expr ) alternative of atomE.

  • GroupByExpression –

    groupByExpression: groupby( selectExpr ).

  • HasClause –

    hasClause: an attribute the entity has a value of.

  • HasTermClause –

    hasTermClause: a glossary term assigned to the entity.

  • Identifier –

    identifier: one ID token, quotes and dots included.

  • IsClause –

    isClause: isa or is (keyword, as written) and a classification.

  • LimitOffset –

    limitOffset: the NUMBER texts of limit and offset.

  • Literal –

    literal; values are the ID texts of a valueArray, empty for the other kinds.

  • LiteralKind –

    Which token or rule a literal is.

  • MaxClause –

    maxClause: max( expr ).

  • MinClause –

    minClause: min( expr ).

  • MultiE –

    multiE: an operand and the products after it.

  • MultiERight –

    multiERight: * or / and an operand.

  • Operator –

    A comparison's operator; the node keeps the spelling it was written with besides.

  • OrderByExpr –

    orderByExpr; sort_order is asc or desc as written, None without one.

  • Query –

    query: its sources (comma_delimited when querySrc is commaDelimitedQueries) and clauses.

  • SelectExpr –

    selectExpr: the expressions of a select or a groupby.

  • SelectExpression –

    selectExpression: an expression and its as label.

  • SumClause –

    sumClause: sum( expr ).

  • WhereClause –

    whereClause.

items.title: aurelius_atlas_lineage_model_client.models
items.text:
The request and response shapes of the lineage-model API (CL-30, LM-01/LM-04; DD-203).

The ids of this module's rules stay here: LineageModelParams is LM-01's query (DV-72/DV-73 are its rejections), LineageModelResponse is the LM-04/LM-01 forward of the data2model answer (DV-68's contract). Field descriptions are the public OpenAPI documentation, so they name no rule ids; the Java classes ported are in the increment spec.

The query of GET / and the answer it forwards from data2model, stated once so the app validates its own query with the same model a caller builds (CL-07). The lineage directions are imported from aurelius-atlas-server-client — the lineage vocabulary belongs to the lineage API (CL-12), not to each consumer; reusing it is CL-10's rule applied to types.

items.title: aurelius_atlas_lineage_model_client.client
items.text:
The async client for the lineage-model API (CL-01..CL-05, CL-30; DD-203, DD-204, DD-205).

The shared client conventions of increment 8.4: constructed from an externally built httpx.AsyncClient and a token source, reading no environment variables (CL-01). The request path is relative, appended to that client's base URL, so a URL with a trailing slash — the str() of a pydantic HttpUrl — works as given (CL-01); the builder closes the pool, the API client never touches its lifecycle. Tests hand over one built on a MockTransport and no socket opens (CL-02); the bearer goes on every call (CL-03); LineageModelClientError rises on a non-2xx answer with the Atlas-shaped body when it parses (CL-04); an unreachable upstream propagates as httpx's own error (CL-05).

The 204 of LM-05/LM-06 — the empty answer, no model — is not an error: it maps to None, the caller's success path (CL-04).

    Where the bearer token comes from: a fixed token, or a callable that yields one (CL-03).

items.title: aurelius-atlas-model
items.text:
Atlas data shapes for Aurelius Atlas, without I/O (DD-002 (the record: specs/0-1-adopt-template/design.md)). Since increment 1.1 (the spec: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-model/specs/1-1-typedef-models/spec.md): the Apache Atlas 2.4.0 type definitions (enum, struct, classification, entity, relationship and business metadata), their header and AtlasTypesDef, as Pydantic models that read and write Atlas's REST JSON. Since 1.5 (the spec: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-core/specs/1-5-builtin-models/spec.md): the patch record AtlasPatch. Since 2.1a (the spec: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-model/specs/2-1-entity-models/spec.md): the entity models of aurelius_atlas_model.instance, one module per Atlas class (AtlasEntity, AtlasEntityWithExtInfo, AtlasEntityHeader, AtlasClassification, AtlasObjectId, EntityMutationResponse, …), and the JSON conventions all models share in aurelius_atlas_model.base. Since 2.1b (the spec: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-model/specs/2-1-value-types/spec.md): Atlas's JSON codec, aurelius_atlas_model.codec, which keeps the digits of decimals.

from aurelius_atlas_model.typedef import AtlasTypesDef

types = AtlasTypesDef.model_validate(request_body)  # Atlas's normalisations apply
response_body = types.to_json()  # Java names, nulls left out, epoch-millisecond dates

from aurelius_atlas_model.instance import AtlasEntitiesWithExtInfo

items.title: aurelius_atlas_model.typedef
items.text:
Atlas type definitions as Pydantic models that read and write Atlas's REST JSON (DD-020).

Ported from org.apache.atlas.model.typedef of Apache Atlas 2.4.0. Field names are snake_case in Python and the Java getter names in JSON (TDM-01). The normalisations the Java setters and constructors apply run as validators, so they hold for request bodies and for models built in code alike.

The TDM-nn rule each class and field ports is cited in the increment spec, not in class docstrings or field descriptions: those are public and end up in the OpenAPI schema, where decision ids mean nothing to a client.

Type Aliases:

  • AttributeDefs –

    attributeDefs: never null, one definition per name (TDM-06, TDM-07).

Classes:

  • AtlasAttributeDef –

    An attribute of a struct, classification, entity, relationship or business metadata type.

  • AtlasBaseTypeDef –

    What every type definition has: identity, audit fields, name and options.

  • AtlasBusinessMetadataDef –

    A business metadata type: attributes that apply to the entity types its options name.

  • AtlasClassificationDef –

    A classification type: attributes, super types and the entity types it may be applied to.

  • AtlasConstraintDef –

    A constraint on an attribute, such as ownedRef or inverseRef.

  • AtlasEntityDef –

    An entity type.

  • AtlasEnumDef –

    An enum type.

  • AtlasEnumElementDef –

    One value of an enum type.

  • AtlasRelationshipAttributeDef –

    An entity attribute that a relationship type adds; read-only, derived from the relationship types.

  • AtlasRelationshipDef –

    A relationship type between two entity types.

  • AtlasRelationshipEndDef –

    One end of a relationship type: the entity type there and the attribute it gets.

  • AtlasStructDef –

    A struct type, and the base of the types that have attributes.

  • AtlasTypeDefHeader –

    The identity of a type definition, as /v2/types/typedefs/headers lists it.

  • AtlasTypesDef –

    Type definitions of every kind: the body of /v2/types/typedefs.

  • Cardinality –

    How many values an attribute or relationship end holds.

  • IndexType –

    How an attribute is indexed.

  • PropagateTags –

    The direction in which classifications propagate over a relationship.

  • RelationshipCategory –

    How the two ends of a relationship depend on each other.

  • TypeCategory –

    The kinds of Atlas types (org.apache.atlas.model.TypeCategory).

items.title: aurelius_atlas_model.codec
items.text:
Atlas's JSON: numbers with a fraction read as decimals, decimals and dates written as Jackson writes them.

Atlas's REST mapper reads floats as BigDecimal (USE_BIG_DECIMAL_FOR_FLOATS) and writes a BigDecimal with its digits and a Date as epoch milliseconds (VAL-01, DD-039).

Functions:

  • dumps –

    Write value as Atlas's REST mapper does, compactly, in UTF-8 (VAL-01).

  • loads –

    Read JSON as Jackson does with USE_BIG_DECIMAL_FOR_FLOATS: every float is a Decimal with its digits.

items.title: aurelius-atlas-otel
items.text: The OTLP ingest credential for the collector's per-service leg (7.18, DD-196), shared by every Aurelius Atlas service that exports telemetry with a Keycloak client-credentials identity (8.0, DD-197).

items.title: Installation

aurelius-atlas-otel = "*"

[tool.uv.sources.aurelius-atlas-otel]
workspace = true

items.title: aurelius_atlas_otel.ingest
items.text:
The OTLP ingest credential for the collector's per-service leg (7.18, DD-196, CIA-07).

The collector's per-service leg (4317 gRPC / 4319 HTTP) accepts only Keycloak client-credentials JWTs minted for the service's realm client otel-<service> (audience otel-collector, the otel-ingest scope). The OTel Python SDK reads OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS statically, and the dev realm's access token lives 60s — a bearer JWT in a static header expires a minute in. So the app owns the OTLP export: a refresh-ahead token source feeds a requests.Session that injects a fresh bearer header on every OTLP request, handed to app-built exporters whose processor/reader setup_telemetry installs on the process's providers (DD-210).

Extracted from the Atlas server's otel_ingest module so every service on the leg shares one credential (8.0, DD-197); the server keeps the settings mapping, this library owns the mechanism.

No new dependency: the session rides the requests the OTLP exporter already uses, and the mint is stdlib urllib. The dev realm's 60s token is why the header is read per request, not once.

items.title: aurelius-atlas-parity
items.text: Parity scenarios for Aurelius Atlas: the scenario format, the runner and the comparison.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
Part of the workspace dev group, which loads the pytest plugin into every test run.

[dependency-groups]
dev = ["aurelius-atlas-parity"]

[tool.uv.sources.aurelius-atlas-parity]
workspace = true

items.title: aurelius_atlas_parity
items.text:
Parity scenarios: requests with the responses Apache Atlas 2.4.0 gives, run against Aurelius Atlas (ADR 052).

Modules:

  • compare –

    The exact comparison of a response body with its expectation (SCN-09, SCN-10, SCN-12; DD-013).

  • path –

    Paths into a JSON document: the JSONPath subset $, .name, ['name'], [n] and [*] (SCN-07).

  • plugin –

    The pytest plugin: gives each scenario test its endpoints and deviations as test properties (SCN-14; DD-014).

  • run –

    Running a scenario: send each stage's request, compare its response, save values (SCN-05 to SCN-12).

  • scenario –

    The scenario format: *.scenario.yaml files, read and validated (SCN-01 to SCN-03; DD-012).

  • testing –

    A sample ASGI application for this library's own tests.

Classes:

  • Scenario –

    One scenario file (SCN-01).

  • ScenarioError –

    A scenario file does not parse or does not match the format (SCN-03).

  • ScenarioFailedError –

    A stage's response differs from its expectation; the message lists every difference (SCN-11).

Functions:

  • load_scenarios –

    Read every *.scenario.yaml below a directory as pytest parameters, one test per scenario (SCN-04).

  • run_scenario –

    Run a scenario's stages in order through the client (SCN-05); {run} is unique to the run (SCN-16).

Read every *.scenario.yaml below a directory as pytest parameters, one test per scenario (SCN-04).

items.title: aurelius-atlas-server-client
items.text: The contract and the async client of the Atlas REST API (8.4, DD-203, DD-204): the admin, types and lineage models every consumer of aurelius-atlas-server speaks, and the httpx2-based AtlasClient that calls it. The lineage-model app imports the lineage wire models from here — one source of truth for both sides of the wire.

[project.dependencies]

items.title: aurelius_atlas_server_client.models
items.text:
The admin and error shapes of the Atlas metadata API (CL-10, 8.4).

The response bodies the server's routes/admin.py and its error handler answer, stated as models so a client can parse them and a test can name them. The typedef bodies are not restated here — they are aurelius-atlas-model's (DD-002), reused whole (CL-10); this module covers only what that library never had: the admin answers, and the {errorCode, errorMessage} body of every Atlas error (SRV-04).

items.title: aurelius_atlas_server_client.client
items.text:
The async client for the Atlas metadata API (CL-01..CL-05, CL-11; DD-203, DD-204, DD-205).

One client per server: constructed from an externally built httpx.AsyncClient and a token source, reading no environment variables (CL-01) — the app builds the httpx client from its own settings (TLS, timeout) and passes it in. The request paths are relative, appended to that client's base URL, so a URL with a trailing slash — the str() of a pydantic HttpUrl — works as given (CL-01); the builder closes the pool, the API client never touches its lifecycle. Because the client arrives from outside, tests hand over one built on a MockTransport and no socket opens (CL-02, the DD-200 seam made async). Every request carries authorization: Bearer <token> from the token source (CL-03); a non-2xx answer raises :class:AtlasClientError with the status and the server's {errorCode, errorMessage} when the body parses (CL-04); an unreachable upstream propagates as httpx's own error — mapping it to an HTTP status is the app's job (LM-07's DV-80), not the client's (CL-05).

The paths mirror the server's routes verbatim: routes/admin.py under /api/atlas/admin (the 8.4 reads plus the 8.11 writes, CLW-01..CLW-07), routes/types.py under /api/atlas/v2/types, the entity routes of routes/entity.py under /api/atlas/v2/entity (CLE-01..CLE-12, 8.9), the glossary routes of routes/glossary.py under /api/atlas/v2/glossary (CLG-01..CLG-09, 8.10), the relationship routes of routes/relationship.py under /api/atlas/v2/relationship (CLR-01..CLR-04, 8.11), the discovery routes of routes/discovery.py under /api/atlas/v2/search (the seven 8.4 searches, CL-13, plus the DSL search and the saved searches, CSD-01..CSD-06, 8.12), and the lineage feed of routes/lineage.py under /api/atlas/v2/lineage (CL-60..CL-63, 8.8).

Type Aliases:

  • GlossarySort –

    The glossary reads' sort parameter (CLG-02, GLS-05).

  • TokenSource –

    Where the bearer token comes from: a fixed token, or a callable that yields one.

Classes:

  • AdminApi –

    The admin resource of an :class:AtlasClient (CL-11): client.admin.

  • AtlasClient –

    The client for one Atlas metadata server (CL-11, DD-203, DD-205).

  • AtlasClientError –

    A non-2xx answer from the Atlas server, with the status and the error body (CL-04).

  • EntityApi –

    The entity resource of an :class:AtlasClient (CLE-01..CLE-12): client.entity.

  • GlossaryApi –

    The glossary resource of an :class:AtlasClient (CLG-01..CLG-09): client.glossary.

  • LineageApi –

    The lineage resource of an :class:AtlasClient (CL-61..CL-63): client.lineage.

  • RelationshipApi –

    The relationship resource of an :class:AtlasClient (CLR-01..CLR-04): client.relationship.

  • SearchApi –

  • TypesApi –

    The typedef resource of an :class:AtlasClient (CL-11): client.types.

Relative to the httpx client's base URL (CL-01): httpx appends them, so the base URL the app passes — trailing slash included, as a pydantic HttpUrl renders one — works as given. LINEAGE_ROOT carries the prefix too (CL-60): the server mounts its feed at /api/atlas/v2/lineage, as every other resource (DD-308).

items.text:
GlossarySort = Literal['ASC', 'DESC']

The glossary reads' sort parameter (CLG-02, GLS-05).

The wire vocabulary is the server's own: routes/glossary.py reads anything but DESC as ascending, so ASC — the default — travels as absence. aurelius-atlas-model's SortOrder is a different vocabulary (ASCENDING/DESCENDING, the search parameter) and is not this one.

The callable shape is 8.2's forwarding (LM-04): a route passes a source that yields the caller's own token, so the client sends the browser's credential upstream.

items.title: aurelius-atlas-trace
items.text: Traceability for Aurelius Atlas: the covers marker, the coverage check and the test report.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
Part of the workspace dev group, which loads the pytest plugin into every test run.

[dependency-groups]
dev = ["aurelius-atlas-trace"]

[tool.uv.sources.aurelius-atlas-trace]
workspace = true

items.title: aurelius_atlas_trace
items.text:
Modules:

  • check –

    The check: every public function and every rule is named by a test (ADR 049 R1, R2).

  • cli –

    The aurelius-atlas-trace command: check and report.

  • config –

    Which projects, packages and specifications the check covers (TRC-07), read from the root pyproject.toml.

  • inventory –

    The public functions of a package: what R1 of ADR 049 says must be named by a test (TRC-06).

  • marker –

    The covers marker: what a test names, validated against the code it names.

  • parity –

    What the check and the report know of parity scenarios: their test properties and the deviations table.

  • plugin –

    The pytest plugin: registers covers, validates it at collection and writes the trace file.

  • report –

    The test report: results, coverage and traceability of one run on one page (ADR 049 R3).

  • rules –

    The rules of the increment specifications: what R2 of ADR 049 says must be named by a test (TRC-08).

  • testing –

    A sample workspace on disk, for tests of the check and the report.

  • trace –

    The trace file: each test's markers and outcome, as the plugin writes it (TRC-11).

Classes:

  • Covers –

    What a test names: canonical function names and rule ids.

  • MarkerError –

    A covers marker names something that is not a function or not a rule id.

Functions:

  • canonical_name –

    Return the defining module.qualname of a function, method or property, or None for anything else.

  • resolve_target –

    Import a dotted path and return the canonical name of the function it names.

Attributes:

  • MARKER_NAME –

  • collect_project –

    Collect a project's tests, without running them, and read their markers (TRC-10).

  • find_gaps –

  • format_findings –

    Describe the findings for a terminal, one item per line.

  • inventory –

    List the public functions of every Atlas project (TRC-06, TRC-07).

  • run_check –

    Collect every Atlas project's tests and compare them with its functions and the specified rules.

items.title: read_rules
items.text:
read_rules(spec_roots: Iterable[Path], enforce_from: Increment) -> dict[str, Rule]

Read the rule ids of every specification from increment enforce_from on (TRC-08).

A rule is a table row whose first cell is a rule id. A specification is either a spec.md in an N-M-slug directory below one of the roots, or a file named N-M-slug.md; other files (the template, the index) are ignored and the search never enters PRUNE_DIRECTORIES. Several files can define the rules of one increment — the parts of a multi-project increment restate their scope — so a repeated id within one increment is one source of truth, and only rows that disagree are an error.

Parameters:

    The rules by id.

items.title: aurelius-atlas-typesystem
items.text:
The Atlas type system for Aurelius Atlas, without I/O (DD-002 (the record: specs/0-1-adopt-template/design.md)): the type registry and the types that type definitions resolve to. Since increment 1.2 (the spec: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-typesystem/specs/1-2-type-registry/spec.md): the built-in, array, map, enum and struct types, attribute types and constraints. Since 1.3 (the spec: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-typesystem/specs/1-3-type-hierarchies/spec.md): entity and classification hierarchies, relationship and business metadata types. Since 2.1b (the spec: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-typesystem/specs/2-1-value-types/spec.md): the value side of the built-in, enum, array and map types, as Atlas checks, normalises and compares attribute values. Since 2.1c (the spec: libs/python/aurelius-atlas-typesystem/specs/2-1-entity-validation/spec.md): the same for structs, classifications (with their validity periods) and entities (with their relationship attributes).

from aurelius_atlas_typesystem.registry import TypeRegistry

registry = TypeRegistry()
with registry.update() as transient:  # committed when the block ends, discarded when it raises
    transient.add_types(types_def)  # resolves every type; raises AtlasError on a bad reference
registry.entity_type("hive_table")

int_type = registry.get_type("int")
int_type.get_normalized_value("42")  # 42; Java's Integer.valueOf rules, None when invalid
registry.get_type("array<int>").validate_value(["x"], "a", messages := [])  # messages: a[0]=x: invalid value…
registry.entity_type("hive_table").validate_value(entity, "entity", messages)  # e.g. mandatory attribute
missing

The type registry and its transient copy (AtlasTypeRegistry, TRG-01 to TRG-09, DD-024).

Readers use a TypeRegistry. Writers take a TransientTypeRegistry from lock_for_update, change it, and release it with or without committing; until the commit, readers see the registry as it was.

items.title: aurelius_atlas_typesystem.types
items.text:
Atlas types: the classes a type definition resolves to, one module per Java class (DD-025, DD-041).

This module re-exports them and makes the unresolved type of a definition (type_of).

Classes:

  • ArrayType –

    array<T> with its cardinality and value counts (AtlasArrayType, TRG-02).

  • AtlasAttribute –

    A resolved attribute of a struct-like type (AtlasStructType.AtlasAttribute).

  • AtlasType –

    A type: its name, category and service type, and how it checks, normalises and compares values.

  • BuiltInType –

    A primitive type such as string or int, of the atlas_core service type (TRG-01).

  • BusinessAttribute –

    A business metadata attribute and the entity types it applies to (AtlasBusinessAttribute, THY-12).

  • BusinessMetadataType –

    A business metadata type: its attributes and the entity types they apply to (THY-12).

  • ClassificationType –

    A classification type: its hierarchy and the entity types it applies to (THY-01 to THY-05, THY-07).

  • EdgeDirection –

    Which way a relationship attribute's edge points (AtlasRelationshipEdgeDirection, THY-10).

  • EntityType –

    An entity type: its hierarchy, relationship and business attributes (THY-01 to THY-06, THY-10 to THY-12).

  • EnumType –

    An enum type: its elements by value and ordinal, and its default (AtlasEnumType, TRG-14).

  • MapType –

    map<K,V> (AtlasMapType, TRG-02).

  • ObjectIdType –

    objectid: a reference to an entity of object_type, by GUID or by unique attributes.

  • RelationshipType –

    A relationship type: its ends, label and the attributes it adds to them (THY-08 to THY-10).

  • StructType –

    A struct type, and the base of every type with attributes (AtlasStructType, TRG-10 to TRG-13).

Functions:

  • entity_types_and_all_sub_types –

    The entity types named and all their sub types (getEntityTypesAndAllSubTypes, THY-07).

  • qualified_attribute_name –

    Type.attribute, or the name itself when it contains a dot or belongs to a root type (TRG-11, THY-05).

  • referenced_entity_type –

    The entity type a type, an array of it or a map to it refers to, or None (TRG-12).

  • type_of –

    The unresolved type of a definition, by its exact class (addTypeWithNoRefResolve).

  • validate_relationship_def –

    Check the ends' cardinality and containers against the category (validateAtlasRelationshipDef, THY-08).

    AtlasBuiltInTypes.AtlasByteType (VAL-04).

    AtlasBuiltInTypes.AtlasDateType (VAL-08).

  • double_type –

    AtlasBuiltInTypes.AtlasDoubleType (VAL-05).

  • float_type –

    What AtlasFloatType and AtlasDoubleType share (VAL-05).

  • int_type –

    AtlasBuiltInTypes.AtlasIntType (VAL-04).

  • integral_type –

    What AtlasByteType, AtlasShortType, AtlasIntType and AtlasLongType share (VAL-04).

  • long_type –

    AtlasBuiltInTypes.AtlasLongType (VAL-04).

  • object_id_type –

    AtlasBuiltInTypes.AtlasObjectIdType (VAL-10).

    AtlasBuiltInTypes.AtlasShortType (VAL-04).

  • string_type –

    AtlasBuiltInTypes.AtlasStringType (VAL-09).

Classes:

  • BigDecimalType –

    bigdecimal: any number, or a string Java's BigDecimal parses, with its digits kept.

  • BigIntegerType –

    biginteger: any number or numeric string, truncated toward zero.

  • BooleanType –

    boolean: a boolean, or true or false in any case.

  • BuiltInType –

    A primitive type such as string or int, of the atlas_core service type (TRG-01).

  • ByteType –

    byte: a 8-bit Java integer.

  • DateType –

    date: a number of milliseconds since the epoch, or a date in Atlas's serialized format, in UTC.

  • DoubleType –

    double: a number within ±Double.MAX_VALUE, held as a Python float.

  • FloatType –

    float: a number within ±Float.MAX_VALUE, held as the shortest decimal of its 32-bit value.

  • IntType –

    int: a 32-bit Java integer.

  • LongType –

    long: a 64-bit Java integer.

  • ObjectIdType –

    objectid: a reference to an entity of object_type, by GUID or by unique attributes.

  • ShortType –

    short: a 16-bit Java integer.

  • StringType –

    string: every value, as Java's text of it.

Attributes:

  • PRIMITIVE_TYPES (tuple[Callable[[], BuiltInType], ...]) –

    The primitive types, string and date, in AtlasTypeRegistry's order; objectid is apart.

items.title: aurelius_atlas_typesystem.java
items.text:
Java's number conversions, on Java values held as Python values (DD-040).

A Java Integer, Long or BigInteger is an int, a BigDecimal a Decimal, a Double a float and a Float a float holding the shortest decimal of its 32-bit value. A bool is a Java Boolean, never a number. Each function is named after the Java method it ports.

Type Aliases:

  • JavaNumber –

Functions:

  • big_decimal_value_of –

    BigDecimal.valueOf(double): the decimal of Double.toString (5 becomes 5.0).

  • double_value –

    Number.doubleValue: the number as Java's double (an infinity beyond its range).

  • float_value –

    Number.floatValue: the number as Java's float (an infinity beyond its range).

  • is_long –

    Whether value is an integer Jackson reads as an Integer or a Long, not a BigInteger.

  • is_number –

    value instanceof Number: an int, float or Decimal, but not a bool.

  • is_valid_time_zone –

    AtlasClassificationType.isValidTimeZone: GMT, or an id TimeZone resolves to another zone.

  • long_value –

    Number.longValue: a BigInteger or BigDecimal wraps to 64 bits; a double saturates, NaN is 0.

  • parse_big_decimal –

    new BigDecimal(String): sign, digits with an optional point, an optional exponent; else None.

  • parse_double –

    Double.valueOf(String): trimmed; sign; decimal or hexadecimal; NaN; Infinity; a type suffix.

  • parse_float –

    Float.valueOf(String): as parse_double, rounded to Java's float.

  • parse_long –

    Long.valueOf(String) and its kin: an optional sign and ASCII digits, or None.

  • time_zone –

    TimeZone.getTimeZone(id), or None for an id Java does not know (EVL-07, DD-042).

  • to_big_integer –

    AtlasBuiltInTypes.toBigInteger: an integer as it is, a decimal or a double truncated toward zero.

  • to_float32 –

    Round a double to Java's float and hold it as the shortest decimal of the 32-bit value (DD-040).

Attributes:

  • DOUBLE_MAX –

    Double.MAX_VALUE.

  • DOUBLE_MIN –

    Double.MIN_VALUE, the smallest positive double.

  • FLOAT_MAX –

    Float.MAX_VALUE, exactly, as a double.

  • FLOAT_MIN –

    Float.MIN_VALUE, the smallest positive float, as a double.

  • SHORT_ZONE_IDS –

    Java's legacy three-letter time zone ids that the tz database lacks, and the zones Java maps them to

items.title: aurelius-atlas-validate-entity-client
items.text: The contract and the async client of the validate-entity API (8.4, DD-203, DD-204): the governance validation card the screen renders and the ValidateEntityClient that asks for it. The aurelius-atlas-validate-entity app imports its own response model from here.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
[project.dependencies]
aurelius-atlas-validate-entity-client = "*"

[tool.uv.sources.aurelius-atlas-validate-entity-client]
workspace = true

items.title: aurelius_atlas_validate_entity_client.models
items.text:
The governance-quality answer of the validate-entity API (CL-40, VE-02; DD-203).

The body the 8.3 mock answers — the four cards the webapp's editor renders, the AppSearchResult<GovQualitySearchObject> shape of the legacy libs/atlas/api::GovQualityApi (ADR 055 R4) — stated as models so a caller parses it and the app's constant is checked against one shape (VE-02, DV-67).

Every leaf is a {"raw": …} wrapper, and the doc-… ids, string compliant flags and _meta.engine of the mock are part of the browser contract, so they are modelled as they arrive, not normalised. The card keys and isNonCompliant are camelCase, the legacy's names.

Classes:

  • GovQualityItem –

    One governance check: a verdict item of a card.

  • GovQualityMeta –

    The _meta of an item: the engine, score and document id.

  • GovQualityValue –

    A {"raw": …} wrapper — every leaf of the governance document is one.

  • ValidationCard –

    One governance card: the items of one aspect, with the card's verdict.

  • ValidationResponse –

    The POST / answer: the four governance cards.

items.title: aurelius_atlas_validate_entity_client.client
items.text:
The async client for the validate-entity API (CL-01..CL-05, CL-40; DD-203, DD-204, DD-205).

The shared client conventions of increment 8.4: constructed from an externally built httpx.AsyncClient and a token source, reading no environment variables (CL-01). The request path is relative, appended to that client's base URL, so a URL with a trailing slash — the str() of a pydantic HttpUrl — works as given (CL-01); the builder closes the pool, the API client never touches its lifecycle. Tests pass one built on a MockTransport and no socket opens (CL-02); the bearer goes on every call (CL-03); ValidateEntityClientError rises on a non-2xx answer (CL-04); httpx's own error propagates on an unreachable upstream (CL-05).

validate posts any mapping — the endpoint never reads the body (VE-01, DD-201), so the request is not a model — and parses the fixed governance document into a :class:~aurelius_atlas_validate_entity_client.models.ValidationResponse (CL-40).

    Where the bearer token comes from: a fixed token, or a callable that yields one (CL-03).

items.title: Installation
items.text:
You can include aurelius-atlas-brand styles in your project by adding them to your root styles.scss file:

@use "@aurelius/atlas-brand/src/main";

Then, you can include the aurelius-atlas-brand assets in your project by adding the following to your angular.json:

{
    "assets": [
        {
            "source": "libs/styles/aurelius-atlas-brand/assets",

        }
    ]
}

Ensure the path points to the correct location of the aurelius-atlas-brand library.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
Aurelius Atlas helps an organisation discover, understand, and trust its data — and stays easy to run, because a catalogue that is expensive to operate governs nothing. The engine behind that is a Python re-implementation of Apache Atlas 2.4.0 with Elasticsearch 9 as its only store. The two working records of the system are the conversion roadmap — the increments, their status and their semantics specs — and the architecture decisions, the ADRs that constrain every change. Both are kept current by every pull request.

What is a 'working record'?

A page that states the system's current truth and is updated by the pull requests that change it — unlike a reference page, which describes a planned state and is written once, by the increment that builds it. If a working record and the code disagree, the record is wrong.

The remaining trees are the reference architecture: they describe the system as it will stand when the plan is done. They are written increment by increment — each page names the increment that writes it, so a page is written in the pull request of that increment, while its facts are fresh (ADR 051). Pages not yet written carry a Planned marker naming their increment; the convention is in Documentation.

Why two kinds of pages

A mid-conversion system has no single accurate description: the code is the plan partly built. Splitting the records (what is true now, maintained by every PR) from the reference (what will be true, written as each increment lands) keeps both statements honest — each page names the increment, spec, or code that owns its facts.

items.title: The trees
items.text:
Tree Subject Written by Vision & Strategy Why the system exists, for whom, and where it is going written (ADRs 046–052, the roadmap) Data Lifecycle Management How catalogue data enters, lives, is shared, and is retired 0.2 → 6.3, per page Data Governance Types, lineage, quality, ownership, auditability 1.6 → 6.2, per page Platform Connectivity, delivery, observability, resilience, security 0.2 → 6.4, per page

Each tree index page carries its own per-page filling map.

These pages state the system's properties by role — the search store, the identity provider, the collector — so the description survives a change of product. The knobs, ports, and commands of each part live in its own documentation: the API Reference pages (design documentation per component), the Contributor Guide (cross-cutting how-tos), and each dev/ slice's README (development topology).

items.title: Decision: self-hosted CI runners on GKE (ARC) vs GitHub-hosted
items.text: Status: decided and live (2026-10-25): Phase 1 canary green 5/5, Phase 2 flipped (devcontainers/ci on GKE), Phase 3 same day - Shape A: the full CI job runs directly in the dev container image on atlas-dev's existing pool (no devcontainers/ci, no dind sidecar, no per-job image pull). Companion to self-hosted-ci.md (the as-built architecture); this doc is the should we, with measured numbers - kept as the decision record.

items.title: TL;DR
items.text:
GitHub-hosted (today) Self-hosted on existing atlas-dev Money, 30-day volume (measured) ~$0–37/mo (plan-dependent) ~$12/mo marginal (pool + cache PVC) Pipeline wall clock green 18m34s equal or better (warm caches, no 10 GB cache eviction) Cache reliability AFD outage broke builds (measured, Sep) plain volumes, no third party Queue / parallelism shared pool, 5×8 GB pulls/jobs own pool, jobs reuse a warm node Ops burden zero ARC upgrades, GitHub App key, GHCR retention Infra cost — none new - atlas-dev already pays the cluster fee

Recommendation: proceed (Phase 1 canary on atlas-dev, ~1 day of work, fully revertible). At our volume the cost is a wash; we buy reliability, speed headroom, and independence. The old blocker ("needs a new Standard cluster, ~€70/mo") is void - atlas-dev is Standard mode.

items.title: Phase 1 result (measured, 2026-10-25)
items.text:
The canary (validate-only, the dev container via devcontainers/ci on an ARC dind runner) ran 5/5 green on atlas-dev's existing default pool - no new node pool, no cache PVC, requests sized to the pool's headroom:

Run Duration Note cold (image built from scratch on the dind sidecar) 9m10s first GKE run, no cache warm (image layers reused) 9m23s concurrent pair (2 jobs on the pool) 14m35s / 14m28s concurrency works within the node warm 9m42s

Findings: the pool carries 2 concurrent jobs comfortably (requests 500m/2Gi each vs 3.92 CPU/13.9 Gi allocatable); image builds on the dind sidecar work (the 100 GB boot disk is ample); idle cost is exactly zero (minRunners: 0, pods scale to zero). Full-pipeline capacity (test fan-out ~6 vCPU / ~30 GB) still exceeds one node, which is why Phase 2 (dedicated tainted spot pool + cache PVC) is the open decision, not Phase 1.

items.title: Phase 2 (live, 2026-10-25) - cache PVC on the existing pool
items.text:
Per the review outcome, Phase 2 ships without new compute: the full CI job moved to the GKE pool via the flag-day variables, on the same default pool, plus a 50 GB PD (RWO) cache volume. The dedicated spot pool stays documented in infra/arc (a commented block) - the first lever if the pool ever runs out of headroom is constraining the dev docker-compose stacks (Elasticsearch/Keycloak heap), not a new node pool.

The cache volume is the ARC runner's work volume (/home/runner/_work), so it is the one path dockerd can bind-mount from that outlives the per-job workspace wipe. Caches bind to /var/cache/ci/* in the dev container - outside the checkout; inside it, dockerd's root-owned bind-mount roots break the next job's git clean (measured, runs 40201875108/40202528986). maxRunners: 1 keeps the RWO volume on one node; CI is serial today, so that costs no throughput.

First measurements (canary + pipeline, this pool): warm npm install 47 s (vs minutes cold); uv cache serves uv sync from the PD within the first minute of container start; queueing behind a busy runner is visible (~6 min serialised) - acceptable at current volume, the Phase 3 levers are the spot pool (parallelism) and Shape A (no 8.3 GB per-pod image pull).

Full pipeline on the pool (run 40210002830, green): 51m13s vs 54m33s before the capacity levers, vs 18m34s hosted. Phase split: setup 5m (image bridge load 13 s, devcontainer build 4.7m), validate 2.5m, test+e2e fan-out 21.5m (node 10.0 Gi / 64 % CPU with the dev-compose caps, vs 13.4 Gi / 101 % without), docker-build+scan+storybook 2.5m, sonar 16.5m (the top tuning target), Chromatic 0.8m. The remaining gap vs hosted is raw compute: the shared pool node (4 vCPU / 13 Gi allocatable, maxRunners 1) vs a hosted 8 vCPU / 32 GB VM per job.

Full pipeline on Shape A (run 40296654173, green 2026-10-26): 41m22s — the first green on the live shape, 10 minutes under Shape B's 51m13s (no image pull, no devcontainer build step, warm actions/cache via the in-cluster cache server, all confirmed in the run log). Landing it took seven GKE-environment fixes after the canary's five green validate runs — the ES coredump-procfs denial (a byte-length-preserving javaagent, tools/es-coredump-agent/), ML's native self-check, the hardened ES image vs a user: override, the sonar-scanner PATH, an inert actions/cache save, elastic's product-check timeout, and the puller restart budget (DD-218) — each root-caused from run diagnostics and documented at the fix site.

items.title: What we measured (30 days, 2026-09-25 → 10-25)
items.text:
Workflow Runs Runner-minutes CI (all jobs, pre-consolidation) 250 3,567 Publish Documentation (PR/main) 327 446 pages, Scan, image builds, deps-bots ~120 ~590 Total ~700 ~4,600

The consolidated CI job (PR 150) is 18m34s green end-to-end; CI volume ≈ 250 runs/month, trending down with consolidation (5 jobs → 1 removes ~4×2m45s of setup per run: 250 × 11 min ≈ 46 runner-min/run saved vs the old shape, already counted in the 18m34s).

items.title: GitHub-hosted (current)
items.text:
Private repos, Linux runners: $0.008/min, included minutes per plan:

Plan Included Overage/mo at ~4,600 min Free (2,000 min) 2,000 ~$21 Team (3,000 min) 3,000 ~$13 Team + self-hosted — $0 (self-hosted minutes are free)

Non-money hosted costs, all observed by us this month:

  • Cache service outage (Azure Front Door) returned HTML 400s and broke every type=gha docker build for hours - we rewired the layer cache to GHCR because of it. The Actions cache (uv/npm/pre-commit) is still the 10 GB LRU pool behind the same service.
  • Per-job overhead: every job = fresh VM = 8.3 GB image pull (~101 s warm) + cache restore + logins ≈ 2m18s; with 250 runs/mo ≈ 575 runner-min paid to setup alone (the single-job shape already cut this 5×).
  • Queue: PR jobs queue behind the shared hosted pool; burst PRs (dep bumps: 274 doc-publishes/mo show the fan-out) don't parallelise on demand.

items.title: Self-hosted on GKE (marginal cost, atlas-dev exists already)
items.text:
Item Europe-west1 est. CI pool: spot n2-standard-8, 0..3, scale-to-zero (250 × 18.5m ≈ 77 h/mo, ~$0.08–0.16/h spot) $6–12/mo Toolchain cache PVC: 50 GB pd-balanced $5/mo ARC controller (2 small pods on existing default pool) ~$1/mo GitHub App, ARC charts $0 GKE cluster fee $0 marginal (paid today for atlas-dev, Standard) Total ~$12/mo

Idle between runs: pool scales to 0; spot nodes are 60–91 % below on-demand. The dev-pool (3× e2-standard-4, ~$80/mo) is not charged to CI - it runs the atlas dev resources regardless.

Break-even vs hosted: self-hosted is cheaper on Free (~$21→$12), neutral on Team (~$13→$12). The case is the reliability/queue/overhead rows above, not the euro-centre.

items.title: Why atlas-dev works (the correction)
items.text:
The plan originally assumed we needed a new Standard cluster (~€70/mo GKE control-plane fee), because an API check suggested atlas-dev was Autopilot (which forbids privileged pods - the ARC dind sidecar is privileged). That check was wrong: autopilot: {} (an empty object, which Standard clusters serialize) was read as "Autopilot". Verified now, three ways:

  1. Console + autopilot.enabled field: absent = Standard.
  2. Node labels: no cloud.google.com/gke-autopilot labels; pool is default-pool (Standard style).
  3. A real privileged: true pod scheduled and ran on atlas-dev (Autopilot rejects it at admission).

So ARC lands on the existing cluster: a dedicated spot CI node pool (tainted ci=true:NoSchedule + nodeSelector - Standard supports both), the controller on the existing pool, a 50 GB PD cache PVC. No new cluster.

items.title: Architecture (one paragraph)
items.text:
ARC (actions-runner-controller, GitHub's official chart) turns each workflow job into an ephemeral pod. The job runs the same pipeline, unchanged, via devcontainers/ci on a per-pod privileged dind sidecar - the exact topology hosted runners use today (that's the bridge we merged: the composite action, ci-pipeline.sh, and the dev container need zero changes). The repo-side flip is four variables (CI_RUNS_ON, CI_DISK_CLEANUP, CI_USE_ACTIONS_CACHE, CI_CACHE_MOUNTS); delete them to revert. Full detail: self-hosted-ci.md.

Superseded by Phase 3 (Shape A, live 2026-10-25): the pod's job container is the dev container image (atlas-ci-runner, the ci-runner devcontainer feature bakes the runner binaries, the docker-in-docker feature supplies the in-image dockerd) - the pipeline and the developer lifecycle scripts run unchanged, directly, in the image developers use. The bridge topology above is retired: the composite action, CI_* variables, and the dind sidecar are deleted (git history has them); runs-on: atlas-ci-shapea is hard-coded in ci.yaml and reverting to hosted is a git revert.

items.title: Risks (honest list)
items.text:
• Privileged dind = root on the CI node. Contained by: dedicated tainted spot pool, jobs are our own code (PRs are the exposure - a malicious PR runs privileged on a CI node, root of that node only; the dev pool is a separate node pool - not node-isolated from data plane blast radius of the same cluster, network policies + node separation are the mitigations). This is the same trust model every self-hosted-dind CI has.
  • Shared cluster: CI pods share the control plane with atlas dev workloads. Worst case (runaway buildkit, node CPU): noisy-neighbour on the CI pool only; control-plane load from ARC is small.
  • Spot preemption mid-run = failed job, requeues. Registry layer cache makes reruns warm. (Measured: zero evictions expected - CI is bursty.)
  • Ops ownership: ARC chart upgrades, GitHub App private key rotation, GHCR buildcache-* retention (already a follow-up). ~a few hours/quarter.
  • Filestore API is blocked in this project (billing-account service restriction): the RWX cache volume is downgraded to a 50 GB PD (RWO) for Phase 1 - serial canaries don't need RWX; Phase 2 adds one PD per node if parallel jobs land on separate nodes.

items.title: Options
items.text:
• A - ARC on atlas-dev (recommended): ~$12/mo, revertible (delete variables + helm uninstall), no new infra. Phase 1 = canary workflow, 5 green runs, then flip.
  • B - Stay hosted (status quo): zero ops, $13–21/mo, keep the AFD cache dependency and per-job pulls. Reasonable at current volume; the queue and 10 GB cache cap are the ceiling.
  • C - Dedicated Standard cluster: the €70/mo scenario - unnecessary now (atlas-dev is Standard). Revisit only if CI's blast radius on a shared cluster becomes unacceptable.
  • D - Shape A (runner pod = the dev container image, no dind sidecar): removes the 8.3 GB per-pod pull (the image is the pod's own container, containerd caches it per node) and the devcontainers/ci layer. SHIPPED 2026-10-25 - this is the live shape. The canary gate ran 3m35s vs 9m+ on Shape B (setup tax gone, 5/5 green), the cache bridge (work dir + caches + containerd store on one PD PVC) brought warm validate to ~81 s, and the full pipeline moved to the direct steps the same day. Shape B (atlas-ci scale set, composite action, CI_* variables, toolchain PVC) uninstalled; the k8s contract that took six trial runs to find (containerd-on-PVC, BuildKit metadata pairing, the work volume at the runner root, JIT registration details) is recorded in infra/arc/README.md.

items.title: Decision asks
items.text:
1. ~~Phase 2: flip the full CI job to GKE (A) or keep it hosted (B)?~~ Resolved 2026-10-25: flipped (A). The flag-day variables are set and the full pipeline runs on the existing pool + cache PVC - no new compute (the review asked for exactly this: PVC first, capacity levers only if exceeded; first lever = constrain the dev docker composes, second = the documented spot pool). Revert = unset the variables + helm uninstall.
  2. ~~GitHub App~~ resolved during Phase 1: the App (atlas-arc) is installed and ready, but runner-management APIs reject App auth on the Team plan - a classic repo-scoped PAT runs ARC today (90-day expiry, rotation = one kubectl command). The App flips back on with an Enterprise upgrade.
  3. ~~Phase 3: adopt Shape A?~~ Resolved 2026-10-25: yes - shipped the same day. The canary gate went 5/5 (3m35s), the cache bridge brought warm validate to ~81 s, and the full pipeline moved to the direct steps; Shape B uninstalled (see option D). Revert = git revert of the ci.yaml flip + helm uninstall atlas-ci-shapea.

items.title: Self-hosted CI on GKE
items.text: Status: as-built (2026-10-26, full pipeline green 41m22s). The ci job runs on self-hosted ARC runners on GKE, directly in the dev container image (Shape A). This is the architecture record; cost/benefit and the option analysis are in self-hosted-ci-decision.md, and the operational how-to (setup, deploy loop, the k8s contract, the PVC layout) is infra/arc/README.md — that file is the source of truth for the mechanics. Scope: the ci job of .github/workflows/ci.yaml. Every other workflow (publish*, scan, rotate-keys, docs, build-devcontainer-image) stays on GitHub-hosted runners — low-frequency, hosted cache service.

items.title: Architecture
items.text:
flowchart LR
    GH[GitHub Actions<br/>workflow job] -->|JIT token| ARC[ARC controller<br/>gha-runner-scale-set-controller]
    ARC -->|creates per job| POD[runner pod<br/>ephemeral, privileged]
    subgraph NODE[GKE atlas-dev default pool]
        POD
        ED[(emptyDir work volume<br/>work + caches + containerd store)]
    end
    POD -->|actions/cache| CS[cache server<br/>20 Gi PD + LRU]
    POD -->|job container IS the image| DC[atlas-ci-runner<br/>dev container<br/>in-image dockerd]
    DC --> GHCR[(GHCR<br/>atlas-ci-runner<br/>buildcache-* tags)]

ARC (actions-runner-controller, GitHub's official chart) turns each ci job into an ephemeral pod whose job container is ghcr.io/aureliusenterprise/atlas-ci-runner — the dev container image developers use. The container command chains the docker-in-docker feature's docker-init.sh (starts an in-image privileged dockerd) to /opt/actions-runner/run.sh; the runner binaries are baked by the .devcontainer/features/ci-runner feature. No devcontainers/ci wrapper, no dind sidecar, no sibling container.
