items.title: Deviations from Apache Atlas
items.text:
Every behaviour of Aurelius Atlas that a client could observe and that differs from Apache Atlas 2.4.0 (ADR 046). The parity report links each tolerated difference to its entry here; a difference without an entry is a defect.

# Area Apache Atlas behaviour Aurelius Atlas behaviour Reason Increment DV-01 Notifications Publishes entity changes to Kafka; consumes hook messages Not supported Out of scope (ADR 050) 0.1 DV-02 Authorization Ranger or simple authorizer Simple authorizer only Out of scope; Ranger needs its own server 0.1 DV-03 Admin version names Apache Atlas 2.4.0 and its build revision Names Aurelius Atlas, its release and its revision A client must be able to tell which implementation answers 0.5 DV-05 Admin The session's timezones are Java's TimeZone.getAvailableIDs() The IANA time zone ids of the server's tz database, sorted Java's list includes legacy three-letter ids the IANA database does not have 0.5 DV-07 Types The built-in model types and the patch records name the operating system account the server runs as Name no user The account is an accident of deployment, and is the same for every type a process loads 1.5 DV-08 Types A patch without an id is recorded, without an id, at every start Is applied at every start and not recorded A record without an id cannot be found again; Atlas never matches it either 1.5 DV-09 Types /v2/types/typedefs and its headers list each kind in the hash order of the registry; of two notsupertype filters, the first in the request parameters' hash order applies Each kind sorted by name; the first notsupertype in the request applies Hash order is not something a client can rely on (DD-034) 1.6 DV-10 Types A write body that is not an AtlasTypesDef is answered by Jersey's JSON provider 400 BAD_REQUEST with Atlas's error body Atlas's source and tests do not state its answer 1.6 DV-11 Types A float attribute given a number beyond the double range fails with NumberFormatException, an internal error The value is invalid for float The failure is an unchecked exception in AtlasFloatType.isValidRange, not a decision; the type treats every other out-of-range value as invalid 2.1b DV-12 Types A date value before year 1 or after year 9999 is valid The value is invalid for date Python's datetime holds years 1 to 9999; such dates do not occur in metadata 2.1b DV-13 Types An entity type given a map without relationship attributes fails with NullPointerException, an internal error The map is checked as one without relationship attribute values The failure is an unchecked exception in AtlasEntityType.validateRelationshipAttributes, not a decision 2.1c DV-14 Admin admin/patches lists the typedef patches and the Java patches that repair JanusGraph and Solr indexes Lists the typedef patches only The Java patches repair indexes Elasticsearch does not have 2.2 DV-16 Entities A request's entities are committed in one graph transaction, never seen half done A reader may see part of a multi-entity write while its bulk request runs; the outcome is all or nothing Elasticsearch has no multi-document transactions (ADR 047, DD-046) 2.2 DV-17 Entities A read by unique attributes given only a unique system attribute (attr:__guid) answers an arbitrary ACTIVE entity of the type Fails with INSTANCE_BY_UNIQUE_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_FOUND Atlas's lookup drops attributes the type does not hold as unique properties and then queries by type alone, an accident of findByUniqueAttributes 2.3 DV-19 Entities bulk/uniqueAttribute answers its entities in the hash order of the attr_<n> indices In the order the indices first appear in the query Java's order is that of a HashMap, which no client can rely on 2.3 DV-20 Entities A write that needs a unique value another entity holds fails with JanusGraph's SchemaViolationException, answered 500 with a plain-text logged id 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with Atlas's error body naming the value and its holder; also for a write that loses two races The plain-text answer hides the cause; a race is retried once (DD-052) 2.4 DV-21 Entities The references of an array, and an array's relationships, are ordered by the hash order of their edges; entities a new reference made updated are reported in a HashMap's order Kept in the request's order, after the relationships that stay; reported in the order reached Hash order is not something a client can rely on 2.4 DV-23 Entities A partial update appending (isAppendOnPartialUpdate) to a stored array or map of references fails with INVALID_OBJECT_ID Appends Atlas maps the stored edges as if they were request values; appending is what the option asks for 2.4 DV-24 Entities A POST without a body, or a bulk write without entities, fails with a NullPointerException, an internal error INVALID_PARAMETERS, as for a null entity or an empty list The failure is an unchecked exception in AtlasEntityStream, not a decision 2.4 DV-25 Entities Deleted and changed entities of a delete are listed in the hash order of the request context's maps In the order they were reached Hash order is not something a client can rely on 2.5 DV-26 Entities Deleting an entity a mandatory reference names fails with a message naming the referring vertex and its graph details Names the referring entity's GUID Aurelius Atlas has no vertices 2.5 DV-27 Entities Every entity referring to a deleted one is changed in the same graph transaction Referring entities are found by a search, which may miss one written at the same moment as the delete Elasticsearch has no incoming edges (DD-057) 2.5 DV-28 Relationships A relationship without end1 or end2 fails with a NullPointerException, an internal error RELATIONSHIP_END_IS_NULL The failure is an unchecked exception, not a decision 3.1 DV-29 Relationships An update without propagateTags fails with a NullPointerException Keeps the stored propagateTags The failure is an unchecked exception in updateTagPropagations, not a decision 3.1 DV-30 Relationships Relationships to one entity are created without touching it Both ends' documents list the relationship, so concurrent writers relating many entities to one retry more often Entity reads stay gets by id (DD-061) 3.1 DV-32 Relationships An inverseRef whose inverse attribute is no relationship attribute is kept as a legacy edge Not maintained Plain references are attribute values (DD-049), and Atlas types since 1.0 use relationships instead 3.1 DV-33 Entities A reference an update drops from an array or map of plain references stays, its edge soft-deleted, and reads back after a soft delete Dropped A plain reference keeps no state of its own (DD-049, DD-058) 2.4 DV-35 Classifications An entity create with a classification of an unknown type fails with a NullPointerException, an internal error CLASSIFICATION_NOT_FOUND The failure is an unchecked exception, not a decision 3.3 DV-36 Classifications bulk/setClassifications with a header without attributes, a type without unique attributes, or no body fails with a NullPointerException or NoSuchElementException The header is skipped as not found, <no unique name> named; no body answers [] The failures are unchecked exceptions, not decisions 3.3 DV-38 Classifications Tasks run one at a time on the active instance, in creation order Every server process runs tasks, each claimed by one, so tasks may run side by side Several processes share the store without a leader (DD-080) 3.4 DV-39 Audit A count, offset or auditAction of {guid}/audit that is not one fails with Jersey's parameter error, answered as a 500 with a text body It fails with BAD_REQUEST A malformed parameter is the client's error; Atlas's answer is its generic mapper, not a decision 3.5 DV-40 Audit Audit events are written in the request before the graph commits; a failed commit leaves events of a change not made Events are written after the change committed; a process stopping in between loses them The audit has its own index, written from the committed entities (DD-082) 3.5 DV-41 Audit A tagUpdateStartTime of bulk/headers that is not a number fails with Jersey's parameter error, answered as a 500 with a text body It fails with BAD_REQUEST A malformed parameter is the client's error, as DV-39 3.5 DV-42 Audit Classification add and update events write the request's classification object, normalised They write the instance as a read answers it Events are recorded after the write, from what is stored (DD-085) 3.5 DV-43 Search LIKE is its in-memory contains and, besides, a pattern of the index or graph query LIKE is contains alone The search is one query (DD-089); the in-memory predicate is the one Atlas applies in every case 4.1 DV-44 Search Named TIME_RANGEs are computed in the server's time zone They are computed in UTC A server's zone should not change what a search finds 4.1 DV-45 Search A marker encodes the hash Java computes of the search parameters It encodes a hash of Aurelius Atlas's own; Atlas's markers are invalid here Java's hashCode is not reproduced 4.1 DV-46 Search classification, query, termName are searched; no parameters or a filter value of another type fail with Java exceptions Until 4.1b, 4.2, 5.2 these fail with BAD_REQUEST; no parameters is INVALID_SEARCH_PARAMS Refusing beats a wrong answer; Java's exceptions are not decisions 4.1 DV-47 Search A wildcard classification name is a regular expression over the entity's pipe-separated names; its * spans names Each name is matched on its own A pattern names one classification 4.1 DV-48 Search A free-text query is read by Solr's edismax: AND, OR, NOT in either case, field:value It is read as simple_query_string: +, \|, - and quotes A malformed query must not fail the search (DD-092) 4.2 DV-49 Search With free text enabled, fulltext searches __fullText, which is no longer written, and finds nothing new fulltext answers from the free text An endpoint that finds nothing helps no client 4.2 DV-64 Interface Serves its own dashboards: dashboardv2 at / and dashboardv3 at /n/ Serves the Aurelius webapp, a web interface of its own design (ADR 053) The product interface is Aurelius's own; the Atlas dashboards stay as the parity reference 7.10 DV-65 Interface No settings control: per-user UI preferences live in the dashboard's UserSettings store, not the header A settings panel (theme, language, time zone, page size, telemetry) opens from the header gear The panel is Aurelius's own interface (ADR 053), stores per browser (DD-161), and touches no Atlas endpoint 7.14 DV-66 Interface No alerts surface: feature toasts, Kafka hook messages to clients An alerts drawer collects app-level alerts (runtime and HTTP errors) The drawer is Aurelius's own interface (ADR 053), touches no Atlas endpoint 7.15 DV-67 Auxiliary API No entity-validation endpoint (the legacy Aurelius app calls a validation service that is itself a mock: it accepts any entity) aurelius-atlas-validate-entity ships the legacy mock contract verbatim, with the workspace's auth and observability The legacy backend is a mock (ADR 055); the browser contract is kept, real validation is a future server rule 8.3 DV-68 Auxiliary API No model-extraction endpoint (the legacy Aurelius app draws lineage via data2model, whose ar3 model comes from the m4i-analytics library: pandas, graphviz, bokeh) aurelius-atlas-data2model reimplements the ar3 output natively; coordinates are deterministic LR-layout numbers, not graphviz positions The browser contract ({model, metadata}) is kept; the legacy library's tree is a retired product's dependency (ADR 055) 8.1 DV-69 Auxiliary API No lineage-flattening endpoint (the legacy Aurelius app flattens Atlas m4i_*_process lineage via lineage_model against its own Atlas) aurelius-atlas-lineage-model reads a configurable Atlas base URL; 8.2 fixtures stand in until the server's lineage feed (5.1) wires it The API ships before its data path so no increment blocks on 5.1 (ADR 055); one upstream setting, no hardcoded host 8.2 DV-70 Auxiliary API data2model renders a null element name as the string 'nan' (pandas' %s of a NaN cell) A null element name yields '' The 'nan' string is a pandas artefact, not a contract; the JSON body carries null as null (DD-198, DTM-02) 8.1 DV-71 Auxiliary API data2model returns its JSON answer as text/html (Flask's dumps and default content type) The answer is application/json; the body contract is unchanged The content type is a Flask accident; the body is the contract (DTM-01) 8.1 DV-72 Auxiliary API lineage_model crashes on an invalid depth/direction query parameter — int()/Enum() raise, Flask answers 500 An invalid query parameter is 400 BAD REQUEST with Atlas's error body Input the request model rejects at the boundary is a client error, not a server fault (LM-07, DD-197 apps) 8.2 DV-73 Auxiliary API lineage_model without a guid fetches the literal guid None (upstream 404, answered 204) A missing guid is 400 BAD REQUEST with Atlas's error body The literal-None fetch is a Flask params.get accident; a required parameter is required (LM-07) 8.2 DV-74 Auxiliary API lineage_model accepts any syntactically present bearer token — @requires_auth(transparent=True) forwards it unvalidated GET / verifies the token for this app's audience (AUX-05) before forwarding it; browser tokens (azp aurelius) pass unchanged An unvalidated pass-through lets a forged token reach Atlas/data2model with the caller's identity; every 8.x app validates its own audience (DD-197); forwarding the raw token is unchanged (LM-08) 8.2 DV-75 Auxiliary API validate_entity accepts any syntactically present bearer token — @requires_auth(transparent=True), and the mock never reads the token POST / verifies the token for this app's audience (AUX-05); nothing is forwarded — the app has no upstreams DV-74's pattern (DD-197): an unvalidated pass-through is pointless on an app with no upstreams, and a forged token gains nothing; browser tokens (azp aurelius) pass unchanged (VE-03) 8.3 DV-76 Auxiliary API The legacy's healthcheck is m4i_backend_core's GET /heartbeat → 200 {"success": true} The healthcheck is GET /liveness → 204, empty body One route, status, and empty body across the 8.x apps' container healthchecks (DD-197 family); no caller reads /heartbeat's body (VE-04) 8.3 DV-77 Auxiliary API lineage_model calls its upstreams bare (requests.post, m4i-atlas-core.get_lineage_by_guid) — every request pays a full timeout while an upstream is down Each upstream is guarded by a circuit breaker (pybreaker, the auth library's convention, AUX-02): outages (5xx, transport) open the circuit, the open circuit answers 502 fast without calling, and a half-open trial closes it The legacy has no resilience device; fast-fail protects the pool and the caller, and the 502 is DV-80's existing wire shape (LM-11..LM-14) 8.5 DV-78 Auxiliary API lineage_model treats the guid as an opaque string — any token is fetched from upstream verbatim (a malformed guid costs a round trip) The lineage chain types the guid as UUID end to end (route query, client models/methods, LineageInfo keys and headers, relation endpoints); a non-UUID guid is DV-73's 400 before any upstream call; relationshipId stays str Atlas guids are UUIDs (Entity.getGuidAsString), so the type is the wire's own shape; pydantic/httpx keep the JSON bytes canonical (format: uuid, lowercase strings) and the extract engine stringifies the rows (LM-01, LM-07, CL-11, CL-12, CL-30) 8.5 DV-79 Auxiliary API data2model answers a malformed extraction body with a Flask ValueError — a 500 A malformed body is 400 BAD_REQUEST with Atlas's error body Input the request model rejects at the boundary is a client error, not a server fault (DTM-11) 8.1 DV-80 Auxiliary API lineage_model lets upstream failures escape — a lineage 5xx, a relation naming a guid absent from guidEntityMap (KeyError), a failing /extract (raise_for_status) all reach Flask as 500 An upstream failure is 502 BAD GATEWAY with Atlas's error body; the caller's token is never leaked into the message A dependency that fails is a gateway condition, and a 500 from uncaught internals is an accident (LM-07) 8.2 DV-81 Search Suggestions are the field's Solr terms: whole values for indexType STRING; ties in any order The analysed words of the text sub-field; ties by term (DD-094) One reading of every field; a stable answer 4.2 DV-82 Search Suggestions of a field that is not a string are its encoded Solr terms There are none Encoded numbers are no suggestion to a user 4.2 DV-83 Search UI A result card fetches its entity lazily on viewport intersection (the App Search answer carries identity only) The card renders straight from the search hit (AtlasEntityHeader.displayText, typeName) The Atlas search contract (SRC-09) answers headers with display text; the per-card GET is dead weight 7.4a DV-84 Search UI The browse cards' explore buttons filter on the m4i governance types (m4i_data_domain, m4i_system, m4i_person); directToUser filters typename: m4i_person with the e-mail as query Business explores typeName=AtlasGlossary, technical explores typeName=Infrastructure; governance searches the signed-in user's plain e-mail, no type filter The m4i types name Aurelius's own type model, which Aurelius Atlas does not ship (ADR 046 keeps Atlas's built-in model); the mappings are model types the server knows — an unknown typeName answers UNKNOWN_TYPENAME (SRC-03) — and the Atlas glossary, not a plain Glossary, is the model's data-domain kind; the e-mail term is the search text Atlas can match 7.4a DV-85 Server AtlasBaseExceptionMapper echoes the exception's message into errorCause on every error status, including 5xx A 5xx answer has no errorCause — the cause's text is logged only — and carries the trace id as requestId (body) and X-Request-Id (header); 4xx answers keep the echo A 5xx cause leaks internals (store URIs, index names, client exception classes) to any caller who can trigger a server fault; the trace id is the support correlation key the OTel pipeline already logs (SRV-07, DD-235) 9.2 DV-86 Server Atlas ships no Content-Security-Policy; the legacy dashboard's inline bootstrap is unscored The dashboard CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' + 'unsafe-eval' scripts and 'unsafe-inline' styles; the JSON API CSP is default-src 'none' — it serves no documents The vendored index.html.tpl inlines the build-varying <%- bust %> value (hashes churn every build), and the require-handlebars-plugin compiles its templates at runtime with new Function (e2e-proven: EvalError kills the boot without 'unsafe-eval'); the strict form returns with the dashboard retirement (6.3) (SRV-08, DD-236) 9.2 DV-87 Server Atlas has no rate limiter: every request is answered, and it has no 429 in its error-code enum The webapp's nginx /api/ proxy limits each public client address (leaky bucket, refusals answered nginx's 429 with an HTML body); the server answers every request it receives, and a caller reaching it directly (internal apps, deployments without the webapp) sees Atlas's answer-everything behaviour Search-cost hardening at the browser's front door (the pentest's M6): a service bursting the API is working, a browser flooding it is attacking, and the webapp arrangement is where the browser is (SRV-09, DD-238) 9.3 DV-88 Search A limit or offset Java's Integer.parseInt cannot read (limit 1e3) escapes as an internal error INVALID_DSL_QUERY, naming the number A number the query got wrong is the client's error 4.3 DV-89 Search DSL operator words (lt, eq, ...) fail with an internal error: the upper-cased word is no operator symbol They compare as their symbols A documented spelling of the grammar should work 4.4 DV-90 Search A DSL number gets L, f or d appended before it is read; a long attribute cannot read it and compares with null The number is read as the attribute's type Comparing a long attribute should find entities 4.4 DV-91 Search A DSL value array is compared as strings Its values are read as the attribute's type Numbers in an array should match numbers 4.4 DV-92 Search DSL like on words matches the index's tokens, the pattern in case against lower-cased words The words of the text sub-field (DD-092), in any case One reading of words for every search; an upper-case pattern should match 4.4 DV-93 Search A DSL query's reason lists every message the composer adds, some following from an earlier one The messages of the rules of 4.4a The follow-on messages depend on the Gremlin composer's internals 4.4 DV-94 Search DSL entities come in the order the graph finds them By creation time, then GUID A stable answer and stable pages 4.4 DV-95 Search hasTerm, arithmetic, aggregates or a bare name as a condition, an expression after isa, a where before any source fail with an internal error, a malformed traversal or no condition INVALID_DSL_QUERY with a reason (hasTerm until 5.2) A client error should say what is wrong 4.4 DV-97 Search A DSL select's rows and groups come in no order (a HashSet, Gremlin's map) Rows in the order of the entities found, groups by their value A stable answer and stable pages 4.4 DV-98 Search A DSL query follows every edge, aggregates and groups every vertex A step that reads every entity found reads at most 10,000 A bounded request (DD-243) 4.4 DV-99 Glossary A glossary list's limit or offset that is no number escapes as an internal error (Integer.parseInt) BAD_REQUEST, as DV-39 A client error should say what is wrong 5.2 DV-100 Glossary Glossaries are listed by Referenceable.qualifiedName, which a glossary lacks: in no order By their qualified name A stable answer and stable pages 5.2 DV-101 Glossary A term's assigned entities are sorted by display text in a copy, then the unsorted set is paged: in no order By display text, paged A stable answer and stable pages 5.2 DV-102 Glossary Removing an assignment the term does not have, or assigning a term to an entity there is not, fails on a null: an internal error INVALID_TERM_DISSOCIATION, RELATIONSHIP_END_IS_NULL A client error should say what is wrong 5.2 DV-103 Glossary An assignment whose status is no AtlasTermAssignmentStatus (DRAFT, ACTIVE) fails every read of its entity's header The meaning without a status One bad attribute should not hide the entity 5.2 DV-104 Glossary A glossary import without a file part, of an unreadable xlsx file or of an empty sheet fails with an internal error; so does an Excel cell that is not text; opencsv takes a backslash as an escape character INVALID_FILE_TYPE, NOT_VALID_FILE, NO_DATA_FOUND; the cell's text; the backslash is kept A client error should say what is wrong; a number is a value 5.2 DV-106 Authentication Any request without credentials but an XMLHttpRequest is redirected to the login page; a 401 carries Jetty's HTML error page A request below /api/ is answered 401 too; a 401 has no body A script or client is told it needs a token, not sent to a page it cannot use 6.1 DV-107 Authentication Every browser request with an unsafe method needs the CSRF header, a bearer-authenticated one too Only a request authenticated by its session cookie needs it A browser sends a cookie unasked, never a bearer token; the webapp sends no CSRF header 6.1 DV-108 Authentication The Keycloak adapter can exchange Basic credentials for a token (enable-basic-auth) No basic authentication; clients obtain tokens from the provider The server never sees a password (ADR 007) 6.1 DV-110 Search Saving or updating without a search, or running a saved search without parameters, fails on a null: an internal error BAD_REQUEST A client error should say what is wrong 4.5 DV-112 Identity One realm serves every shape of the deployment Two realm shapes: clusters install the hardened aurelius-atlas realm (no seeded users, real hosts, ROPC off, PKCE S256); the dev compose and the four e2e suites keep the master realm (localhost origins, ROPC, demo users) and realm.name: master stays a supported cluster escape hatch The browser-login test rig and the production identity surface want opposite settings; importing the app as Keycloak's admin realm was the pentest H3 finding, and the split keeps the rig intact (DD-273) 10.7 DV-113 Identity One Grafana auth posture everywhere The cluster's Grafana logs in through the realm (confidential grafana client, Viewer default with client-role escalation); the dev compose's Grafana keeps the anonymous-Viewer posture, and the grafana client exists only in the prod realm asset — CHT-79's first named parity exception A local dashboard over local telemetry needs no IdP, and a client the dev stack never uses is drift bait; the pentest H4 exposure is a cluster fact, and DD-275 records the exception so the parity guard still catches unintentional divergence 10.8 DV-114 Authorization Privileges are granted by a policy of regular expressions over types, entities, classifications and labels, per user and group (atlas-simple-authz-policy.json, or Ranger) By four fixed roles of the server's client in the identity provider Who may do what is managed in one place, the identity provider (DD-300) 6.2 DV-115 Authorization Type definitions are validated before their privileges are checked Their privileges are checked first: an invalid definition from a user without them is refused as unauthorized The checks sit at the endpoint, before the store 6.2 DV-116 Entities An entity's labels, and those a label audit event lists, come in the hash order of a HashSet In the order first given: a set's labels as given, an add's new labels after the entity's own (DD-021) Hash order is an artefact of Java's set, not a meaning; the given order is stable and readable 5.3 DV-117 Entities An entity's business metadata, its attributes, and the business metadata an audit event tells, come in the hash order of HashMaps In the order of the entity type's business metadata and of each one's attributes Hash order is an artefact of Java's maps; the type's order is stable 5.3 DV-118 Entities Adding or updating business attributes with a business metadata given as null, or businessmetadata/{bmName} without a body, fails on a null value: an internal error Taken as that business metadata given no values A null map is a client's way of saying none; failing on it helps no one 5.3 DV-119 Entities A business metadata import applies and lists its entities in a HashMap's order; an import without a file part fails on the missing part In the order the file first names them; no file part is FILE_NAME_NOT_FOUND Hash order is no meaning; a missing file is a client error, as a blank file name is 5.3 DV-120 Import/export An export answers Content-Encoding: gzip for a ZIP it does not compress further; an export without a body fails on the null request No Content-Encoding; no body is an empty request A client that decodes the declared gzip breaks on the ZIP; an empty request is the client's meaning 6.3 DV-121 Import/export An export's type definitions, metrics and the starting entities found by value come in the hash order of sets and maps In the order first met Hash order is no meaning; the order met is stable 6.3 DV-122 Import/export An export item of type hdfs_path that does not exist is created (HdfsPathEntityCreator) Not created; the item fails The catalogue has no HDFS model, and an export should not write 6.3 DV-123 Import/export An import's classification events come before the entity's ENTITY_IMPORT_UPDATE, in the same transaction After it, each a write of the classification store (DD-305) The classification store keeps the one copy of the removal and propagation rules 6.3 DV-124 Import/export An imported shell entity (isIncomplete) that is not stored is created as a shell vertex Created as a full entity Exports from a catalogue without hooks hold no shell entities 6.3 DV-125 Import/export admin/importfile reads the ZIP of any path the server can read Only from the server's configured import_folder; any other name is not found A path named by a request must not open the server's file system 6.3 DV-126 Import/export An imported entity whose unique values a stored entity holds renames that entity to the imported GUID, recording the old one; an entity retried after the rest is retried from the position after it The stored entity keeps its GUID, the imported GUID standing for it during the import (DD-306); the entity itself is retried Our documents name entities by GUID; a rename rewrites them all 6.3 DV-127 Import/export An import's transformers option changes entities through AtlasEntityTransformer and the Hive and HDFS entity handlers The option is not applied The handlers rewrite Hive and HDFS models the catalogue does not hold; the transforms option covers the generic rewrites 6.3 DV-128 Import/export An incremental export of hive_db or hive_table extracts through IncrementalExportEntityProvider, and an import of one replicates table deletions (TableReplicationRequestProcessor) The generic incremental fetch; no table replication Both serve Hive replication only 6.3 DV-129 Import/export A removeClassification transform of an entity without classifications fails on the null list The entity is left as it is A failed import for nothing to remove helps no one 6.3 DV-130 Import/export admin/expimp/audit fails on an entry the user may not read: the scrubbed entry has no times to unbox The entry is left out A reader's missing privilege should hide what it cannot read, not fail the list 6.3 DV-131 Import/export An export or importData whose items include one named by GUID alone fails on the null type name when its admin audit counts the items by type, after the operation ran The item is counted in resultCount but not by type The operation succeeded; its audit should not turn it into an error 6.3

items.title: Java to Python Map
items.text: Where each part of Apache Atlas 2.4.0 goes. Updated by every increment; the status column is the truth about what has been ported. items.title: Spec Map
items.text:
Where each increment's specification lives: <home>/specs/<N-M-slug>/spec.md, with its DD-NNN records in design.md beside it. The home is the project that owns the increment's rule namespace; when an increment's rules are split across two projects, both parts are named and they share the one rule table (the trace tool reads them as a single source, so a shared row repeated at different tree depths is the same rule). The columns after the home list the rule namespaces.

This table is the reference for a move: it fixes the home before files are touched. A move PR changes the Status column and nothing else here. Homes follow ADR 002 : a rule belongs to the project whose code it constrains.

items.title: Increments
items.text:
An increment's semantics specification lives in the project it touches: it is written before the code (ADR 051) as <project>/specs/N-M-slug/spec.md, with its DD-NNN records in design.md beside it. An increment that spans two projects gets one part per project, sharing the rule table; the increment-to-project map is Spec Map.

The pages below are the specifications written before the move: kept here as history until their series moves. Copy the template to start a new one, add its project's specs directory to the specs roots in the root pyproject.toml, and keep its status in step with the roadmap.

items.title: 5.3c Business metadata import
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: to follow
  • Records: DV-119; relies on DD-302, DV-104 (the file reading of 5.2d), DV-117

The last part of 5.3 imports business attribute values from a CSV or Excel file. Each row names an entity by type and unique value, a business attribute as <business metadata>.<attribute>, and a value. A template gives the header line. The file is read as the glossary import reads it (5.2d). The values are applied through 5.3b's add-or-update with overwrite, so they are validated, audited and checked as there.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Endpoint Atlas method GET /api/atlas/v2/entity/businessmetadata/import/template produceTemplate POST /api/atlas/v2/entity/businessmetadata/import importBMAttributes

In aurelius-atlas-core, EntityBusinessMetadata.bulk_create_or_update_business_attributes and business_metadata_headers. In aurelius-atlas-model, FILE_NAME_NOT_FOUND. In aurelius-atlas-server, the two routes in routes/entity.

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule BMI-01 The template is the line EntityType,EntityUniqueAttributeValue,BusinessAttributeName,BusinessAttributeValue,EntityUniqueAttributeName[optional], an application/octet-stream download named template_business_metadata BMI-02 The import takes the form's file; a blank file name is FILE_NAME_NOT_FOUND (404), and the file is read as GIM-01 reads it. Each row below the header, numbered from 2, fails with a reason when it misses a type, unique value, business attribute or value (Line #<n>: missing fields. [<cells>]), names no entity type, names an attribute the type does not have or one that is not unique (the fifth cell, else qualifiedName), names no entity of exactly that type with that value, or names no business attribute of the type BMI-03 A value of an array attribute is split at \|. Each element is parsed by the element type: int, long, short and date as whole numbers in range, float and double as Java parses them, boolean as true in any case, an enum as one of its values; any other as text. An element that fails is left out and reported with Atlas's text (Provided value <v> is Integer of Long type at line #<n-1>, and the like). A value of any other attribute is the cell's text BMI-04 Each entity named is given its stored business attributes with the rows' values set, and overwritten with them (BMD-04). The response lists the rows that failed, then each entity that failed, its GUID and its business attributes as Java's map text ({bm={attr=value}}), with the error's message; it lists each entity that succeeded the same way with SUCCESS BMI-05 An entity's overwrite is checked as BMD-04's (AUZ-17); a refusal is that entity's failure, not the import's

items.title: 5.3b Business metadata
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: to follow
  • Records: DD-302, DV-117, DV-118; relies on DD-052, DD-084, DD-300, DD-301

Business metadata types (1.x) declare attributes that apply to chosen entity types. This part stores their values on entities. An entity can be given them when it is created and reads them back. They are added, updated, overwritten and removed by their own endpoints, validated against their definitions, audited, and checked with the privilege 6.2b left for 5.3. Their CSV import follows in 5.3c. Searching on them is not part of 5.3.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Endpoint Atlas method POST /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid}/businessmetadata?isOverwrite= addOrUpdateBusinessAttributes DELETE /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid}/businessmetadata removeBusinessAttributes POST /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid}/businessmetadata/{bmName} addOrUpdateBusinessAttributes DELETE /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid}/businessmetadata/{bmName} removeBusinessAttributes POST /api/atlas/v2/entity, /bulk; GET /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid} businessAttributes of an entity

In aurelius-atlas-core, entity_business_metadata (EntityBusinessMetadata and the mapping functions), the business attributes of a read in entity_retriever, of a created entity in entity_writer, their notification and audit event. In aurelius-atlas-server, the four routes in routes/entity.

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule BMD-01 The endpoints by GUID take a JSON object of attribute values by business metadata; those by name take the attribute values of that business metadata. No body is none; any other body is BAD_REQUEST (DV-10). isOverwrite is true only for true in any case. Each answers 204 without a body BMD-02 An entity's business attributes are those of its type's business metadata with a value, by business metadata and attribute name, in a full read's businessAttributes, absent when there is none (DV-117). A created entity takes those it is given of its type's business metadata, each mapped as an attribute value is; a business metadata, attribute or null value its type does not have or need is left out. An update leaves them as they are BMD-03 Adding or updating needs a GUID and a non-empty object (INVALID_PARAMETERS) and the entity (INSTANCE_GUID_NOT_FOUND). Every problem is then reported at once (INSTANCE_CRUD_INVALID_PARAMS): a business metadata its type does not have, a value invalid for its attribute, a string longer than the attribute's maxStrLength, and a mandatory attribute without a value given or stored. Each attribute given is set; a null sets the attribute's optional default, removing a string. A value that stays is not counted as a change BMD-04 With isOverwrite, every business attribute of the entity's type becomes the value given, and one given none is removed; a mandatory attribute must be given. The entity is written at the request's time and user even when nothing changes BMD-05 Removing needs a GUID, a non-empty object and the entity. Each attribute named is removed, or every attribute of a business metadata given no values. Each counts as a change, with or without a value BMD-06 A change that is written tells the audit a BUSINESS_ATTRIBUTE_UPDATE for each business metadata it changed, Updated business attributes: then a struct's JSON of the business metadata's name and the values given its changed attributes, null for one removed. A created entity's come after the classifications it is given, before the next entity's and before the creates AUZ-17 Adding or updating needs ENTITY_UPDATE_BUSINESS_METADATA for each business metadata of the entity's type whose values change, add/update business-metadata: guid=<guid>, business-metadata-name=<name>, before validation: one given null counts only when overwriting, and one whose given and stored values are both empty, or equal, does not count. Removing needs it for each business metadata named, remove business-metadata: guid=<guid>, business-metadata=<name>

items.title: 5.3a Labels
items.text:
• Status: in progress
  • Pull request: to follow
  • Records: DV-116; relies on DD-021, DD-052, DD-084, DD-300, DD-301

An entity's labels are free words a steward attaches to it. They are stored with the entity since 2.4 (EWR-09), can be searched (__labels), and are returned on every read. This first part of 5.3 serves the endpoints that set, add and remove labels, records what each change did in the entity's audit, and checks the label privileges that 6.2b left for this increment. Business metadata follows in 5.3b, and its CSV import in 5.3c.

items.title: Scope
items.text:
Endpoint Atlas method POST /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid}/labels, .../uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}/labels setLabels PUT /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid}/labels, .../uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}/labels addLabels DELETE /api/atlas/v2/entity/guid/{guid}/labels, .../uniqueAttribute/type/{typeName}/labels removeLabels

In aurelius-atlas-core, entity_labels (EntityLabels), the label notifications of entity_change_notifier and their audit events in entity_audit_listener, and the labels of a created entity told by entity_writer. In aurelius-atlas-server, the six routes in routes/entity.

items.title: Semantics
items.text: Id Rule LBL-01 Each endpoint takes a JSON array of labels, or no body for none; any other body is BAD_REQUEST (DV-10). A label given twice counts once. Each answers 204 without a body. By unique attributes, the typeName is checked for length and must be an entity type (TYPE_NAME_INVALID), and an entity must hold the attr: values (INSTANCE_BY_UNIQUE_ATTRIBUTE_NOT_FOUND) LBL-02 Setting labels needs the entity (INSTANCE_GUID_NOT_FOUND) and valid labels: at most 50 characters (INVALID_LABEL_LENGTH) of letters, digits, _, - or CJK characters (INVALID_LABEL_CHARACTERS, its quotes taken as escapes by MessageFormat). The entity's labels become those given, none for no body or an empty array. The entity is written with the request's time and user even when its labels stay LBL-03 Adding labels needs at least one (INVALID_PARAMETERS, labels is null/empty), the entity and valid labels. The labels the entity does not have are appended; when it has them all, nothing is written LBL-04 Removing labels needs at least one, the entity and valid labels. The labels the entity has among them are removed; when it has none of them, nothing is written. An entity left without labels has none (null stored, [] read) LBL-05 A change that is written tells the entity's audit what it removed, LABEL_DELETE with the details Deleted labels: and the labels, each after a space, then what it added, LABEL_ADD with Added labels: and the labels, each only when there is one. Creating an entity with labels records its LABEL_ADD before the classifications it is given and its ENTITY_CREATE AUZ-16 Setting labels needs ENTITY_ADD_LABEL for each label added, add label: guid=<guid>, label=<label>, and ENTITY_REMOVE_LABEL for each removed, remove label: ..., checked once the labels are validated. Adding needs ENTITY_ADD_LABEL for each label given, add/update label: ..., and removing ENTITY_REMOVE_LABEL for each given, remove label: ..., both checked before the labels are validated. Nothing is written when a check refuses

items.text:
Apache Atlas release-2.4.0:

  • webapp/.../web/rest/EntityREST.java: setLabels, addLabels, removeLabels (by GUID and by unique attributes)
  • repository/.../store/graph/v2/AtlasEntityStoreV2.java: setLabels, addLabels, removeLabels
  • repository/.../store/graph/v2/EntityGraphMapper.java: setLabels, addLabels, removeLabels, updateLabels, validateLabels, createVertexWithGuid (the labels of a created entity)
  • repository/.../store/graph/v2/AtlasEntityChangeNotifier.java: onLabelsUpdatedFromEntity
  • repository/.../audit/EntityAuditListenerV2.java: onLabelsAdded, onLabelsDeleted

items.title: Deviations
items.text:
• DV-116: Atlas keeps labels in a HashSet, so an entity's labels, and those an audit event lists, come in the set's hash order. Aurelius keeps them in the order first given (DD-021): a set's labels after those the entity had, an add's new labels after the entity's own.

Atlas writes each audit event under a key of the entity, the millisecond and the event's place in its batch; two events of one label change in the same millisecond share a key, and HBase keeps the second. Aurelius keeps both. Their order between themselves is then not defined, so the scenario reads them by action.

items.title: Specification Template
items.text:
Copy the block below into N-M-short-slug.md and fill it in before writing code.

# N.M Increment title

- **Status:** planned | in progress | in review | done
- **Pull request:** link
- **Records:** ADR / DD numbers this increment adds or relies on

## Scope

What this increment delivers: endpoints, operations, projects. Then what it explicitly does not
deliver, with the increment that will.

## Semantics

Each rule the behaviour must obey, in plain words, with an id that tests name in
`@pytest.mark.covers(..., rules=["XXX-NN"])`.

| Id     | Rule |
| ------ | ---- |
| XXX-01 |      |

## Java origin

The Atlas classes (2.4.0) whose behaviour this ports, so reviewers can compare.

## Deviations

Deliberate differences from Apache Atlas, each added to [Deviations](../deviations.md).

## Acceptance

The parity scenarios and test files that prove the rules, and how to run them.

items.title: Data Governance
items.text:
Governance in the terms the business uses: people discover and understand data, know who is accountable for it, see how it flows and how sensitive it is, and can prove all of it. Concretely, that is how Aurelius Atlas describes, classifies, connects, and accounts for data — the catalogue's own subject: the type system, lineage, glossary, classifications, and audit trail. The rules live in the increment semantics specs; these pages assemble them into the governance view.

Page Scope Written by Roles & Responsibilities Who owns and who may act: authorizer roles, dataset ownership 6.2 (ADR 042) Data Dictionary The type system as the catalogue's dictionary: typedefs, built-in models, inheritance 1.6 (material exists from 1.1–1.5) Data Quality Glossary, terms, business metadata, labels as quality signals 5.2, 5.3 Data Lineage Processes, inputs/outputs, depth and direction, on-demand lineage 5.1 Compliance & Auditability Entity audit events, classifications with validity, audit REST 3.5, 6.2 Every page here is Planned — where do I read the rules?

In the increment specs, which are written with the code and are the authority (semantics specs); the dictionary's material, for example, exists from increments 1.1–1.5 even though its page lands with 1.6. A Planned marker names the increment whose spec to read instead.
